# MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide

*Updated October 20, 2026 | English instructions | EN/RU interface*

> **Applicability.** This guide is verified against the current implementation and the live public/login entry for the **MoveFlew application** [1]. Staff procedures reflect the current menus, forms, and backend rules; the published route map [2] is used for current navigation labels. Where this guide says configuration, activation, consent, or provider verification is required, the workspace owner must complete it before that third-party function is treated as available.

> **Verification boundary.** The procedures describe the implemented controls and recorded states. They do **not** claim that authenticated end-to-end card/ACH transactions, external email/SMS delivery, QuickBooks transmission, camera/device operation, provider activation, or native schedule registration were performed while preparing this guide.

## How to use this manual

Start with **Getting Started** to sign in, select the right workspace, and learn the role-aware sidebar. Then follow the operating flow appropriate to your work: sales and estimates → dispatch → field execution → finance, storage, and reporting. Use **Troubleshooting & FAQ** before repeating a blocked action or escalating an issue.

**Global operating rules**

- Confirm the active workspace and your role before creating, editing, or interpreting any record. Sidebar visibility is role-aware; server permissions remain authoritative.
- Use the exact current sidebar labels. In particular: **Merchant gateway** is `/app/payment-gateway`, **Transactional messaging** is `/app/transactional-messages`, and **Claims & settlements** is `/app/claim-settlements`.
- A preview, copied link, browser redirect, scheduled state, or success page is not automatically a saved business outcome. Read the page’s success/error notice and reload the record or ledger when the workflow says to verify it.
- Do not create workspaces, users, jobs, memberships, or financial records merely to explore. Do not paste card/bank details, credentials, API keys, webhook secrets, or customer tokens into notes or escalations.
- The **Language / Язык** selector changes interface labels and locale formatting between English and Russian. It does not translate customer-entered text, move dates, change stored money, or prove a provider’s state.

## Contents

1. [Getting Started & Dashboard Navigation](#1-getting-started--dashboard-navigation)
2. [Sales, Quotes & Lead Management](#2-sales-quotes--lead-management)
3. [Operations, Dispatch & Long-Distance Trips](#3-operations-dispatch--long-distance-trips)
4. [Crew On-Site Workspace (Field & Drivers)](#4-crew-on-site-workspace-field--drivers)
5. [Storage, Vaults & SIT Management](#5-storage-vaults--sit-management)
6. [Billing, Payroll, Expenses & Claims](#6-billing-payroll-expenses--claims)
7. [Reports, Marketing & Webhooks](#7-reports-marketing--webhooks)
8. [Troubleshooting & FAQ](#8-troubleshooting--faq)

## 1. Getting Started & Dashboard Navigation

### What this chapter covers

This chapter explains how staff sign in, choose a workspace, read the **Overview** dashboard, switch language, use the role-aware sidebar, and use the available **Settings** administration tools.

**Prerequisites and roles**

- You need a Manus account. The CRM uses Manus sign-in; there is no separate CRM password.
- A user with no workspace can create one. To work in an existing workspace, your Manus account must already be a member (or an Admin must link your already-signed-in account).
- Workspace roles are **Admin**, **Office admin**, **Sales & estimator**, **Dispatcher**, and **Field crew**. The server remains the final authority for permissions, so a visible menu item does not guarantee that an action will be accepted.
- Do not create a workspace, member, or test record merely to explore. Ask the workspace owner/Admin to perform setup when appropriate.

### 1. Sign in with Manus

1. Open the team login page at `/login` (the public route is titled **Team login**).
2. If the session is still being checked, wait for **Checking your session…**. If you are already signed in, select **Open your workspace**.
3. If you are not signed in, select **Continue with Manus**. Complete the Manus sign-in flow.
4. Use **Back to home** to leave the login page. For help, use **Need a hand? Contact the crew**.
5. After sign-in, the login page identifies the account as **Signed in as {account}** and offers **Open your workspace**.

**Success state:** the workspace application opens and loads the selected company. If there is no selected workspace, the setup page appears instead.

**Note:** **Secure account login. No extra password to remember.** is an explanatory message, not a second login method.

### 2. Choose, create, or change a workspace

#### Choose an existing workspace

1. After Manus authentication, the application loads your memberships. The first available membership is selected by default unless a previously selected workspace is still valid.
2. In the left sidebar, select the current workspace button (building icon, company name, and your role).
3. In the menu, select the company you need. Each option shows the workspace name and your role there.
4. Wait for the application to reload. The workspace name in the top breadcrumb and the records on the page now belong to the selected company.

**Success state:** the active workspace button and the top bar show the new workspace; the sidebar role can also change because roles are membership-specific.

#### Create a new workspace

Use this only when you are intentionally starting a new company workspace and have owner approval.

1. On **Set up your workspace**, enter a name in **Workspace name** (required; at least 2 characters). The placeholder example is **e.g. MoveFlew**.
2. Select **Create workspace**. The button is disabled until a non-blank name is entered and shows **Creating…** while saving.
3. The new workspace is selected automatically and the application reloads.

**Success state:** the new workspace opens empty. The page explicitly says that no demo customers are created.

**Limit—no self-service “join workspace” screen:** the current onboarding does not offer a join-code field or a general **Join workspace** action. If you need access to an existing company, ask its Admin to link your Manus account from **Settings → Membership** after you have signed in once (see the **Settings** instructions below). Do not create a second workspace as a workaround.

### 3. Switch English/Russian and understand persistence

1. Find the language selector with the globe icon. On login and onboarding it is in the top area; inside a workspace it is in the top bar.
2. Open the selector labelled **Language / Язык**.
3. Choose **English** or **Русский**. This manual is intentionally written in English; the product selector can switch the interface to Russian.
4. The choice is saved in the browser, so it remains selected across reloads and later visits in that browser. Date/number formatting follows the selected locale (English uses the US locale; Russian uses the Russian locale).

**Tip:** if labels look unfamiliar, switch back to **English** before following this chapter. The language selector is available on the login, workspace setup, and workspace shell.

### 4. Navigate with the role-aware sidebar

The sidebar groups links and hides links that are not assigned to the current role. On a narrow screen, use **Open navigation**; close it with **Close navigation** or select a destination. The active destination is highlighted.

The current grouped labels and links are:

- **Workspace:** **Overview**.
- **Sales & customers** (office roles—Admin, Office admin, Sales & estimator, Dispatcher): **Leads**, **Sales pipeline**, **Estimates**, **Tariff engine**, **Communications**.
- **Moving operations:** **Jobs** (all roles); management roles (Admin, Office admin, Dispatcher) also see **Dispatch**, **Calendar**, **Warehouse scanner**, **Trip planning**, **Fleet & crew**, **Resource availability**, and **Storage**; office roles see **Inventory catalog**; field-enabled roles (Admin, Office admin, Dispatcher, Field crew) see **Field crew**; all roles see **Job documents**.
- **Finance & service:** management roles see **Move invoices**; finance roles (Admin and Office admin) also see **Billing & payments**, **Expenses**, **Payroll & tips**, **Claims**, **Merchant gateway**, **QuickBooks accounting**, and **Claims & settlements**.
- **Growth & insights** (office roles): **Reports**, **Marketing**, **Reviews**.
- **Administration** (finance roles): **Integrations & API**, **Transactional messaging**, **Automations**, **Settings**.

**Exact route notes for linked tools:** the sidebar’s current implementation uses `/app/payment-gateway` for **Merchant gateway**, `/app/transactional-messages` for **Transactional messaging**, and `/app/claim-settlements` for **Claims & settlements**. Use these links when opening the tools directly.

**Role-specific behavior to remember:**

- **Field crew** can see **Jobs**, **Field crew**, and **Job documents**, but the application blocks Field job sheets for an **estimator** with the message **Field job sheets are available to dispatch, office admins, and assigned crew members.**
- The dashboard’s **New estimate** action is not shown for **Field crew**.
- **Settings** is shown only to finance roles. Within it, Admin and Office admin can use pricing and sequence settings; a Dispatcher can use the membership tab as a read-only crew directory when the page is reached through an available route or permission.

### 5. Read the Overview dashboard correctly

Select **Overview** (the dashboard route is `/app/dashboard`). The page heading is **Overview** and the caption identifies the selected workspace.

The four headline metrics are calculated from saved workspace records:

1. **Open opportunities** — customer records whose status is not marked won, closed, or inactive. The hint is **Customer records needing attention**.
2. **Scheduled moves** — jobs whose status is not complete or cancelled. The hint is **Across all upcoming dates**; this count is not limited to a chosen calendar range.
3. **Estimated revenue** — the sum of saved job `total` values. The hint is **From saved estimate totals**.
4. **Open invoice value** — the sum of each job’s `finalTotal` (or `total` when no final total is present) when the invoice status is not marked paid. The hint is **Based on invoice status**.

Use the dashboard panels as follows:

- **Revenue from saved jobs** groups job totals by move month, plus **Unscheduled**, and displays the most recent six groups. It says **Totals reflect estimates and completed invoices.** If there are no saved jobs, the success/empty state is **No revenue history yet**.
- **Upcoming moves** shows up to five non-complete/non-cancelled jobs whose move date is today or later, ordered by move date and start time. Select a row to open that job; use **All jobs** to open Jobs. If none qualify, the state is **No upcoming moves**.
- **Follow-ups** shows up to five incomplete reminders, with their due date/time. **Manage** opens Leads. If none are due, the state is **Nothing due**.
- **Dispatch readiness** reports the number of saved fleet vehicles and saved people records in the workspace. These are record counts, not a live statement that vehicles or people are currently available.

**Date semantics:** “upcoming” includes a move dated today and later. The dashboard does not provide a date-range picker. Revenue uses each saved job’s move month; an unscheduled job is grouped separately. The displayed date/time is localized by the English/Russian selector and the browser’s date formatting.

**Quick actions:** **View leads** opens Leads. **New estimate** opens the estimate creation route and is hidden for Field crew. These buttons navigate; they do not themselves save a lead or estimate.

### 6. Use Settings for rates and team membership

Open **Settings** from Administration when your role is allowed. The page displays **Your role: {role}. Server permissions remain authoritative.** Its tabs are **Pricing**, **Membership**, and **Sequences**.

#### Pricing: maintain workspace rates

Pricing is for Admin and Office admin. It is labelled **Rates & materials** and explicitly says **Editable workspace configuration; this is not a published tariff.**

1. Select **Pricing**.
2. Review or enter the six mover-rate fields: **1 mover (no truck)** and the five remaining mover-count fields (the labels are generated as mover counts).
3. Review or enter **Minimum hours**, **Packing hourly rate**, **Weekend markup %**, **Travel per mile**, **Weight rate**, and **Mile rate**.
4. In **Material matrix**, review each material name and price. The current screen edits the existing rows; it does not provide an add/remove material control here.
5. Select **Save pricing**.

**What the button does:** it writes the complete rates/materials configuration for the active workspace and reloads the saved values. **Success state:** **Pricing settings saved.**

**Validation constraints:** the server requires exactly six hourly rates for one through six movers; rates and most amounts cannot be negative. **Minimum hours** must be from 2.5 through 24. Weekend markup is limited to 0–500%; the other rate fields have server maximums. If a value is rejected, read the displayed error and correct the field—do not assume a save occurred.

#### Membership: view members or link a signed-in user

1. Select **Membership**. The **Workspace membership** table lists **Member**, **Role**, and the current member’s name/email.
2. Admins can change a member’s role using the role selector. The change saves immediately when the selector changes and the table refreshes.
3. Admins can use **Link signed-in user**. Enter the person’s address in the email field (placeholder **person@example.com**), choose a role, and select **Link member**.
4. The page reports **Membership link saved.** after a successful link and refreshes the member list.

**Required prerequisite:** the person must have signed in with Manus before an Admin can link the email. The screen says **People must have signed in before their email can be linked.** If not, the server returns **This user must sign in first before they can be added to the workspace**. An already-linked address cannot be added twice.

**Role and safety constraints:** only Admin can add members or change roles. Office admins can view the membership directory but cannot edit roles or add members. At least one workspace Admin must remain; the server rejects a change that would remove the last Admin. There is no remove-member control in this screen.

**Limit—no join codes:** the current Membership UI provides **Link signed-in user**, not a generated join code or invitation URL. The safe supported alternative is: have the person complete Manus sign-in, then have a workspace Admin link the exact signed-in email and role. Do not promise that **Membership link saved.** sends an email invitation; it records the membership link in the workspace.

#### Sequences

**Sequences** is present as a Settings tab and is subject to the same Admin/Office admin restriction as pricing. If your role is not permitted, the page displays: **Pricing and sequence settings are available to Admin and Office Admin. Dispatchers can use the Membership tab as a read-only crew directory.** Do not treat a disabled or blocked tab as a missing record; ask an Admin/Office admin to perform the configuration.

### 7. Profile area and sign out

The bottom of the sidebar shows the signed-in user’s name (or **Signed-in user**) and role. The top bar shows the signed-in email beside the account icon. The current implementation does not provide an editable profile form in the workspace shell.

To leave the account:

1. Select the sign-out icon in the sidebar. Its accessible label/title is **Sign out**.
2. Wait for the session to end. The application returns to the sign-in flow; use **Continue with Manus** to authenticate again.

**Tip:** signing out does not delete the workspace or its records. Switching workspace changes the active company; it does not copy or merge data between companies.

### Troubleshooting and safe limits

- **Workspace loading:** wait for **Opening your workspace…**. If an error appears, use the offered retry action rather than creating another workspace.
- **No workspace listed:** this means the signed-in account has no membership. Use the Admin linking procedure above; there is no join-code fallback in this implementation.
- **Wrong company data:** check the active workspace switcher and breadcrumb before editing anything. Workspace selection is persistent in the browser, and each company’s records are kept separate.
- **Missing sidebar item:** verify the current role and use the role-aware list above. Do not navigate by guessing an unavailable route.
- **Provider/configuration wording:** pages such as **Merchant gateway** and **Transactional messaging** are navigation tools/configuration areas. This chapter makes no claim that a payment, messaging, accounting, or other provider is active. Owners select providers and configure them later.

### Next workflow

Once your access, workspace, and rates are ready, continue with [Sales, Quotes & Lead Management](#2-sales-quotes--lead-management). Dispatch and crew assignment are covered separately in [Operations, Dispatch & Long-Distance Trips](#3-operations-dispatch--long-distance-trips).

<!-- help:quick-tasks:start -->
## Quick-Task Reference

| Action | Direct route | Minimum reference role | Operational note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Build & Send Quote | [`/app/estimates/new`](/app/estimates/new) | Sales & Estimator | Sales staff can build and share a proposal link; automated sending needs configured office messaging and consent. |
| Daily Crew & Truck Dispatch | [`/app/dispatch`](/app/dispatch) | Dispatcher | Eligible driver, skill, availability, and acknowledged warnings are required. |
| On-Site Job Sheet & Signatures | [`/app/field`](/app/field) | Field Crew | Field crew must have an active linked crew profile and assignment to the job. |
| Storage Vault Intake | [`/app/storage`](/app/storage) | Office Admin | Dispatchers can also perform physical intake under the current role rules. Billing remains finance-only. |
| Monthly Storage Invoices | [`/app/billing`](/app/billing) | Admin / Office Admin | Generate invoices writes records, not customer charges; billing cycles are duplicate-protected. |

Roles are not a single seniority ladder. These reference roles do not replace workspace permissions: authorized office staff can perform supported tasks, dispatchers can also perform physical storage intake, and field crew access stays limited to assigned moves.
<!-- help:quick-tasks:end -->

## 2. Sales, Quotes & Lead Management

This chapter covers the sales record from first lead through estimate, proposal, customer review, and (when staff explicitly changes the job) booked status.

### Prerequisites, roles, and language

- Sign in to the correct workspace and confirm the workspace name and role in the header. The top-bar selector can switch the interface between **EN** and **RU**; this manual is intentionally English-only.
- Sales records are available to **Admin**, **Office admin**, **Sales & estimator**, and **Dispatcher** roles. **Field crew** can access only the areas exposed to that role and cannot create or edit sales leads.
- The **Tariff engine** and **Transactional messaging** pages are office-only. Tariff profile import is an **Admin** action. Integration keys, portal links, and provider setup are restricted to **Admin** and **Office admin**.
- A route lookup needs exact origin and destination addresses. A licensed tariff calculation needs an owner-provided, attested carrier profile; NW Crew does not seed a universal tariff table or call a tariff vendor.

### 1. Create and maintain a lead or customer

1. In the sidebar, open **Sales & customers → Leads**. Alternatively, open **Sales pipeline** for a visual stage board.
2. Select **Add lead**. In the form, **Full name** is required. **Email**, **Phone**, **Source**, **Stage**, **Fit score**, and **Notes** are available; **Fit score** accepts 0–100. The normal initial stage is **lead**.
3. Select **Save lead**. The record returns to the saved list. To change it later, use the row’s **Edit lead** action and save again. Use **Add reminder** when a dated follow-up is needed; both the reminder title and **Due date & time** are required.
4. In **Leads**, use **Search name, email, phone** and **All stages** to narrow the list. The table shows customer, stage, source, score, and the next open reminder.

**Tip:** The separate **Sales pipeline** page searches name, email, phone, or source and adds a **Minimum score** filter. Drag a card to another column or use its stage selector; a successful move saves the customer stage immediately.

#### Pipeline stages and loss handling

The actual pipeline stages are **lead**, **qualified**, **estimate**, **booked**, **won**, and **lost**. In the legacy Leads editor, the visible choices may be **lead**, **qualified**, **estimate sent**, **won**, and **lost**; use the label shown in the screen you are using.

**Limit — loss reasons:** There is no implemented **Loss reason** field, loss-reason list, or separate loss-reason report. To preserve context, put the explanation in **Notes** before selecting **lost**. Do not invent a separate reason workflow.

### 2. Capture consent, ownership, tags, and attribution

1. Open **Sales & customers → Sales pipeline**, select a lead card, and open **Lead details**. (The same preference controls are also available from **Communications** after selecting a customer.)
2. In **Contact preferences and attribution**, set **Email consent**, **SMS consent**, and **Opted out** accurately. Select **Assigned team member** or leave it **Unassigned**. Only eligible workspace members appear. Add labels in **Tags (comma separated)**.
3. Expand **UTM and custom tracking** and enter the canonical fields **source**, **medium**, **campaign**, **content**, **keyword**, **adGroup**, and **customTracking**. Save with **Save lead**. Preferences and attribution are saved with the customer record.
4. Treat **Opted out** as controlling: do not use an outbound channel when the customer has opted out. Consent is evidence for messaging controls, not permission to claim that a provider is active.

### 3. Build a quick estimate in four steps

1. Open **Sales & customers → Estimates → New estimate**. The wizard has four steps: **Customer & move**, **Exact route**, **Household inventory**, and **Pricing & proposal**.
2. **Customer & move:** enter required **Customer name**; add **Email**, **Phone**, **Move title**, **Move date**, and **Move size**. The available size choices are **Studio**, **Apartment**, **2 bedroom**, **3 bedroom**, **House**, and **Office**. Select **Continue**.
3. **Exact route:** enter **Origin address & ZIP** and **Destination address & ZIP**. Select **Get exact route**. On success, the wizard displays miles and minutes and uses them in pricing. If lookup fails, correct both exact addresses and retry.

   **Limit:** No substitute distance is invented when the Maps lookup fails. Do not rely on an unreturned route value.

4. **Household inventory:** search with **Find household items**, then use each item’s minus/plus controls. The running total shows cubic feet and pounds. The picker consumes the approved tenant catalog; quantities become part of the estimate.
5. **Pricing & proposal:** choose **Pricing method**: **Hourly local move** or **Long distance (weight + miles)**.
   - Hourly: set **Crew size**, **Hourly rate**, and **Estimated labor hours**. The configured minimum-hours rule applies to the calculation.
   - Long distance: set **Weight rate / lb** and **Mileage rate**; inventory weight and route miles feed the base amount.
   - Both methods support **Route travel fee**, **Packing labor hours**, **Packing materials**, and named **Accessorial name** fees. Enter a fee name (for example, a long carry), then enter its amount. The preview lists each fee. Add **Pickup / move notes** when conditions need to be recorded.
   - Review **Proposal preview** and **Estimated total**. A weekend adjustment can appear when configured for the workspace.
6. Select **Save & create proposal**. The button creates the job/estimate record and a shareable proposal token, then opens the saved job. **Saving** indicates the request is in progress; the saved job page is the success state.

### 4. Use a managed inventory catalog

1. Open **Moving operations → Inventory catalog**. This is the tenant-managed source for canonical inventory items used by pickers and estimates.
2. Select **Add catalog item** or **Edit**. Required fields are **Item key**, **Canonical item name**, **Room**, **Per-unit cubic feet**, and **Per-unit pounds**. **Item key** must contain only letters, numbers, underscore, or hyphen. Keep **Active in inventory picker** checked when the item should be selectable.
3. Select **Save catalog item**. The list shows the key, canonical item, room, per-unit estimates, and active/inactive status.

**Important:** Volume and weight are per-unit planning estimates, not certified measurements or a guaranteed quote. Deactivating an item removes it from future picker choices; it does not silently rewrite an existing signed quote.

### 5. Review, copy, and send a proposal; understand booking

1. From **Estimates**, select **Open** on a saved estimate, or open the job from the estimate wizard’s success page.
2. On the job page, review **Move plan**, **Estimate**, and **Proposal**. Select **Open shareable proposal** to open the public proposal. The customer can review and e-sign there.
3. To share the link, select **Share proposal**. A success notice says **Proposal link copied.** If clipboard access is unavailable, copy the proposal URL from the browser address bar.
4. The Proposal card states **Customer e-signature received.** or **Awaiting customer signature.** A signature records proposal acceptance; it is not by itself a booking transition.
5. To change the operational status, choose **draft**, **estimate**, **booked**, or **cancelled** in the status selector and select **Save status**. Choosing **booked** is the actual booked transition and can queue the `job.booked` business event. It is not triggered by merely opening, copying, or signing the proposal.
6. **Assign dispatch** opens **Assign truck & crew** for management roles. It validates driver eligibility, skills, and schedule conflicts before saving. Assignment is operational allocation, not the sales-stage change.

**Limit — no automatic “customer signed = booked” action:** There is no separate customer-facing “book now” transition in this sales flow. After acceptance, an authorized office/management user must review the record and explicitly save **booked**.

### 6. Use the owner-attested Tariff engine (licensed profile workflow)

Open **Sales & customers → Tariff engine**. Office roles can select a job and preview; only **Admin** can import a profile.

#### Import a profile (Admin only)

1. In **Owner-attested JSON import editor**, select **Load blank template** if needed.
2. Replace every `REPLACE` value with the carrier’s licensed/published data, including carrier identity, jurisdiction, effective dates, tariff reference, and rules/bands. Set `licenseAndSourceAttested` to true only after owner review.
3. Select **Import attested JSON**. A success notice states the owner-attested profile was imported and is available for server previews. Editing or loading the text alone creates no business row.

**Limit:** The page explicitly says this is not a universal 400N calculator. It does not seed a 400N table, call a tariff vendor, or imply carrier authority. Owners must select the licensed profile now and configure/replace the source later where necessary.

#### Preview and freeze

1. In **Job selector**, enter a positive **Job ID** and select **Open job**. The route is `/app/tariffs?job=ID`; selecting a job only loads its current frozen revision.
2. Select an active profile and enter **Service date**, **Origin state**, **Destination state**, **Crew size**, **Estimated hours**, **Shipment weight (lb)**, **Distance (mi)**, **Trips**, **Travel miles**, **Stair flights**, **Elevator stops**, and **Elevator wait (minutes)**. Optionally enter **Heavy-item code (optional)** and **Heavy-item quantity**.
3. Select **Preview server quote**. Review **Preview line items**, effective ranges, approved hourly rate, minimum labor, and total. Preview alone never changes the job.
4. If the values or profile change, preview again. The **Freeze on unsigned job** button is enabled only when the current preview matches the current inputs and the job is not signed/completed.
5. Select **Freeze on unsigned job**. The success notice states that a frozen tariff revision was applied to the unsigned job and linked draft estimate. The resulting **Current frozen snapshot** shows revision, profile version, lines, and total.
6. If a snapshot already exists, check **I intentionally want a new revision of the existing frozen quote.** before creating a deliberate revision. Later profile or approved-rate edits do not rewrite the frozen snapshot.

**Hard constraint:** If the job is signed or completed, the screen displays **Signed or completed — changes blocked** and tariff changes cannot be applied.

### 7. Quote embed widget, keys, UTM, and public links

1. Open **Administration → Integrations & API** and use the **Embed forms** tab. A widget requires an active **widget** access key. Select **Create access key**, enter required **Name**, choose **Kind: widget**, and select **Create key**.
2. A widget key is restricted to `leads:create`. After creation, copy the one-time token, **Browser-relative link**, and **Iframe code (uses this browser origin)** from the secret dialog. The success dialog says the token cannot be retrieved again; select **I copied it** only after storing it in the approved secure location.
3. The public route is `/quote/<one-time-token>` and is titled **Embedded quote intake**. The widget creates a lead request; it does not book a move or create a signed estimate by itself.
4. UTM and custom attribution are canonicalized on the saved lead through the fields in **UTM and custom tracking**: `source`, `medium`, `campaign`, `content`, `keyword`, `adGroup`, and `customTracking`. Review or correct these fields on **Lead details** after intake.

**Limit — origin controls:** The current **Embed forms** UI provides the key, relative link, and iframe code based on this browser origin; it does not expose a separate staff-facing allowed-origin list. Do not promise domain allowlisting that is not shown.

### 8. Customer portal, inventory review, invoices, and deposits

1. In **Integrations & API**, select **Create access key**, choose **Kind: portal**, and select the required **Bound customer**. Portal keys must be customer-bound and expose only that customer’s data. The fixed scopes are `portal:read` and `portal:inventory:submit`.
2. Select **Create key**, then copy the one-time **Browser-relative link** from the secret dialog. The public route is `/portal/<one-time-token>`; the **Portal links** tab lists the bound customer but intentionally does not reveal the token again.
3. The customer portal can show **Jobs and proposals**, **Invoices and balances**, **Storage**, and **Documents and recorded terms**. A customer can select **Open proposal** for a linked proposal.
4. Under **Inventory for staff review**, the customer selects a **Linked job**, adjusts quantities for the canonical items already on that job, and selects **Submit for staff review**. A success notice states the selection was submitted; it does not change a signed estimate or booking.
5. For an invoice with an eligible balance (at least the implementation’s minimum checkout amount), the portal offers **Pay in TEST checkout**. It opens a test checkout in a new tab.

**Limit — deposit/invoice reality:** The portal exposes linked invoice balances and TEST checkout, not a separate “deposit invoice” creation button in this sales chapter. Returning from TEST checkout does not mark an invoice paid; only a verified payment webhook updates status. Owners must configure the merchant provider later; do not claim that payment is live or that a deposit was collected.

### 9. Communications and transactional messaging

#### Record a conversation safely

1. Open **Sales & customers → Communications** and choose a customer in **Select a saved customer**. The activity list can be filtered by **All channels** / **All directions**, or by `note`, `call`, `email`, `sms` and `inbound`/`outbound`.
2. In **Record communication**, choose **Channel**, **Direction**, optionally **Related job (optional)**, and enter the required **Record** text. Select **Save manual record** for notes, calls, or inbound records.
3. For outbound email/SMS, the button changes to **Save blocked draft**. Saving records the attempt but does not send it. With consent it is recorded as `blocked_not_connected`; without consent it is blocked for no consent. The success notice explains that no connected delivery provider was used.
4. In **Consent and preferences**, update **Email consent**, **SMS consent**, or **Opted out of contact**, then select **Save preferences**. Consent must be recorded before any later provider-controlled send.

#### Configure templates and consent gates

1. Open **Administration → Transactional messaging** (the real route is `/app/transactional-messages`, not `/app/messaging`). The page is for office staff; crew cannot use it.
2. In **Provider policy**, choose **Email provider** (SendGrid or Amazon SES), set **Enable transactional email** and/or **Enable consented SMS**, then select **Save policy**. Availability is reported as **Email ready** and **SMS ready**; owners must configure credentials, verified senders, and callbacks later.
3. In **Recipient consent**, select **Customer**, choose **Channel**, enter **Consent evidence / source**, and check **Customer agreed to transactional messages**. For SMS, record **Customer also agreed to review-request SMS** when applicable. Check **Documented re-opt-in after STOP, if applicable** when supported by evidence, then select **Record consent**. Customer and source are required for this action.
4. In **Create a template**, select **Business event** and **Channel**, enter **Subject** for email and **Plain-text body**, then optionally check **Enable this template for future events**. Available tokens include `{{companyName}}`, `{{customerName}}`, `{{jobTitle}}`, `{{moveDate}}`, `{{invoiceAmount}}`, `{{proposalUrl}}`, `{{portalUrl}}`, and `{{reviewUrl}}`. Select **Save template**.
5. Select a customer and use **Preview for selected customer** to render the content. The success notice says **Preview only — no message sent.** Use **Enable** or **Disable** beside a saved template to change future-event eligibility.
6. For a permitted business event, enter **Resource ID: job ID, invoice ID, or move-JOBID** and select **Queue selected event**. This queues the event under consent and provider controls; it is not proof of delivery. **Process eligible queue** is an Admin action and requires confirmation; review the **Submission & delivery history** status and provider reference/error afterward.

**Provider gate:** Saving a template, recording consent, previewing, or queuing an event does not prove that a message sent. The UI explicitly distinguishes accepted/queued from delivered. Do not claim active email/SMS providers, delivery, or automatic retries unless the actual status and provider configuration confirm it. For owner setup, use **Merchant gateway**, **Transactional messaging**, and other linked tools from **Integrations & API**; configure later rather than entering invented credentials.

## 3. Operations, Dispatch & Long-Distance Trips

This chapter covers the workspace tools used to prepare resources, assign scheduled moves, and group booked jobs into multi-day long-distance trips. The sidebar is role-aware: if a label is not shown, the current role cannot use that tool.

### Prerequisites and roles

1. Sign in to the NW Crew workspace and select the correct workspace from the workspace switcher.
2. Use an **Admin**, **Office admin**, or **Dispatcher** role for dispatch, trip planning, fleet/crew maintenance, and resource availability. These controls are not available to estimators or field crew.
3. Before assigning a truck, create at least one truck and an active crew member in **Moving operations → Fleet & crew**. A truck assignment must include at least one eligible driver.
4. Before planning a trip, create or book the jobs. Trip planning only lists jobs with status **booked**, **in_progress**, or **completed**; an estimate is not enough.
5. Keep dates, duration, inventory, crew skills, and truck limits accurate. Server validation is authoritative even when a card can be dragged on the screen.

### Prepare trucks and people in Fleet & crew

Open **Moving operations → Fleet & crew** at `/app/fleet`. The page has two tabs: **Fleet (count)** and **Crew (count)**.

#### Add or edit a truck

1. Select the **Fleet (count)** tab and choose **Add truck**. To change an existing record, use its pencil edit control.
2. Complete the truck form:
   - **Truck name** — required.
   - **Plate** — optional.
   - **Capacity (cu ft)** — required, non-negative.
   - **Weight limit (lb)** — required, non-negative.
   - **Dimensions** — optional; the placeholder is `L × W × H`.
   - **Status** — **active**, **maintenance**, or **inactive**.
3. Select **Save truck**. The form saves the record and the Fleet table refreshes. **Cancel** closes without saving.
4. Use capacity and weight values as operating limits. Dispatch checks saved job inventory against both limits; an over-capacity assignment is not silently accepted.

#### Add or edit a crew member

1. Select the **Crew (count)** tab and choose **Add crew member**. Use the pencil edit control to update an existing person.
2. Complete the form:
   - **Name** — required.
   - **Email** and **Phone** — optional contact fields.
   - **Linked signed-in team member** — optional. Choose **Unlinked field profile** or a signed-in member. Linking makes that person’s assigned jobs appear in **Field crew**; it does not by itself make the person dispatchable.
   - **Skill level** — required, from 1 through 5.
   - **Hourly rate** — required, non-negative.
   - **Team role → Authorized driver** — check this when the person is eligible to drive a truck.
   - **Status** — **active** or **inactive**.
3. Select **Save crew member**. The saved person appears in the Crew table with role, skill, rate, linked user, and status. **Cancel** closes without saving.
4. For a truck assignment, at least one selected crew member must be an active authorized driver. Every selected crew member must be active and meet the job’s required skill level.

### Dispatch timeline: daily truck and crew lanes

Open **Moving operations → Dispatch** at `/app/dispatch`. This is the current daily assignment tool and is separate from the prior Calendar view.

1. Set **Move date**. The page loads a daily **Truck and crew Gantt** with a 24-hour axis and 15-minute slots.
2. Review **Unassigned backlog**. It contains active jobs missing a truck or any crew. Cancelled and completed jobs do not appear as active backlog work.
3. Review truck lanes under **Trucks** and people lanes under **Crew**. Existing jobs show on their assigned resource lanes. A lane also shows the resource status.
4. For pointer users, drag a job card from **Unassigned backlog** or a scheduled lane onto a truck or crew lane. For keyboard/accessibility use, select the card and use the **Assignment form** instead. Dragging changes the draft only; it does not save immediately.
5. In **Assignment form**, confirm or edit:
   - **Job** — select the job and customer.
   - **Move date**.
   - **Start time** — 15-minute increments.
   - **Duration (hours)** — 0.25 to 24 hours, within one calendar day.
   - **Truck** — choose a truck or **Backlog / no truck**.
   - **Crew** — select one or more crew checkboxes. Authorized drivers are marked `driver`.
6. Select **Preview assignment**. The server checks the current job/resource state and returns either no warnings or warning acknowledgements. A successful no-warning preview displays **No dispatch warnings. Confirm to save this assignment.** and **Server preview passed with no soft overlap or capacity warnings.**
7. If warnings appear, read each **Dispatcher acknowledgement required** item and check it only after reviewing the operational consequence:
   - **The truck overlaps another scheduled job.**
   - **One or more crew members overlap another scheduled job.**
   - **Selected inventory exceeds this truck’s configured capacity or weight limit.**
8. Select **Confirm dispatch**. This button stays disabled until every displayed warning is acknowledged. On success, the notice **Dispatch assignment saved.** appears and the timeline reloads.
9. Preview again whenever the job, selected resources, or overlapping schedule changes. The confirmation is tied to that exact server preview; a stale preview is rejected.

#### Dispatch constraints and safe responses

- A completed or clocked-in job cannot be rescheduled. A cancelled job cannot be dispatched. Open the job record and use the appropriate operational process instead of trying to force an assignment.
- An inactive, maintenance, out-of-service, or unavailable truck cannot be assigned. Select an active truck or update the fleet record first.
- Inactive crew, insufficient skill, missing eligible driver, and resource-availability blocks are hard stops, not acknowledgement warnings. Correct the resource or date and preview again.
- Truck/crew overlaps and capacity excess are soft warnings in this current timeline flow. A dispatcher must explicitly acknowledge each one before **Confirm dispatch** becomes available; acknowledgement does not override hard stops.
- If another user changes the job after preview, the server asks you to refresh/re-preview. Do not retry a stale confirmation.
- The saved assignment also refreshes the job’s crew links and queues the dispatch business message. It does not claim that an external messaging provider is active.

### Prior Calendar view (separate tool)

The same **Moving operations** group also contains **Calendar** at `/app/calendar`. It remains a date-oriented planning view and is not the current Gantt workflow.

1. Use the **Daily**, **Weekly**, or **Monthly** tabs.
2. Change the date with the date picker or the buttons labelled by accessibility text **Previous calendar period** and **Next calendar period**.
3. In Daily view, resource rows show **Truck / crew resource** lanes. In Weekly/Monthly view, jobs appear in calendar day cells.
4. Dragging to a calendar day relocates the job while retaining its start time. Dragging to a truck row changes the vehicle; dragging to a crew row adds that person without removing already assigned crew.
5. The server remains final: overlap, driver, skill, status, capacity, and availability checks can reject the drop. Read the displayed error and correct the assignment in the current **Dispatch** assignment form when possible.
6. Use **Open jobs** to reach `/app/jobs` for the job record. A calendar drop is not a substitute for preview/acknowledgement in the current Dispatch Gantt.

### Resource availability blocks

Open **Moving operations → Resource availability** at `/app/operations`. This is the durable block tool; a block prevents planning resources only after the server accepts the requested range.

1. Select **Block resource**. The button is unavailable when the workspace has neither a crew member nor a truck.
2. In **Block resource availability**, choose **Resource type** (**crew** or **truck**).
3. Choose the named **Resource**. Changing the resource type refreshes the resource list.
4. Set **From date** and **To date**. The end date cannot be earlier than the start date.
5. Enter a **Reason**; it is required.
6. Select **Save block**. On success, the modal closes, the table refreshes, and **Unavailability block saved.** appears. **Cancel** closes without creating a block.
7. Review the **Resource unavailability** table, which shows **Resource**, **From**, **To**, and **Reason**. To remove a future restriction, select **Revoke**; the success state is **Unavailability block revoked.**
8. Use **Refresh** when another operator may have changed blocks. A non-revoked block covering a selected dispatch date hard-stops assignment. Trip planning also rejects a selected truck or driver unavailable during any part of the trip range.

The same page includes **Scheduled job capacity**. It calculates each active job’s saved inventory volume and weight, shows truck limits when a truck is assigned, and reports **within limits**, **over capacity**, or **limits unavailable**. For an unassigned truck it says **Assign a truck to compare limits.** These figures are operational checks, not estimates.

### Plan a long-distance trip

Open **Moving operations → Trip planning** at `/app/trips`. Trip plans group existing jobs and resources; they do not reschedule their jobs.

1. Select **Plan a trip**. To start another plan while editing an existing one, select **New trip**.
2. Enter a required **Trip name** (up to 180 characters).
3. Set required **From date** and **To date**. The end date must be on or after the start date.
4. Choose a **Status**: **Planned**, **Dispatched**, **Completed**, or **Cancelled**.
5. Under **Booked jobs**, check the jobs to include. Only **booked**, **in_progress**, and **completed** jobs are offered. Every selected job’s move date must fall inside the trip range; the server rejects jobs outside it.
6. Under **Trucks**, check one or more trucks. The list shows capacity and status. If there are no trucks, create them in **Fleet & crew** first.
7. Under **Eligible drivers**, check active crew members marked as authorized drivers. If no one appears, mark a suitable person **Authorized driver** in **Fleet & crew** and keep the person active.
8. Add optional **Trip notes** (up to 5,000 characters).
9. Review the notice: trip plans do not move job dates, while resource conflicts are warnings requiring explicit acknowledgement; normal dispatch still enforces job-level assignment rules.
10. If the trip overlaps another trip’s truck or driver commitment, review the displayed **Truck overlaps trip: [name]** or **Driver overlaps trip: [name]** warning. Check **I have reviewed overlapping trip commitments and explicitly approve any resource conflict.** only when the conflict is intentional.
11. Select **Save trip**. The success state is **Trip saved.** and the plan appears under **Planned trips** with a **Trip summary**, range, status, linked trucks, drivers, jobs, warnings, and notes.
12. A **Dispatched** trip must include at least one job, one truck, and one driver. The server also requires selected trucks to be available and selected drivers to be active and eligible. A resource-availability block is a hard rejection, not something the acknowledgement checkbox can override.
13. To revise a saved plan, select **Edit trip**, make the changes, and save again. The edit resets the acknowledgement checkbox, so review conflicts again.
14. Select **Print trip summary** on the relevant trip card to print that trip’s summary. Other trip cards are hidden for printing; printing is a record/output action and does not dispatch or reschedule anything.

### Frozen dates, signatures, and tariff repricing

Moving a job to another date through current dispatch can trigger repricing because date-sensitive pricing is recalculated for the new date. There is an important safety lock:

- A **signed** move or a move with a stored tariff-rate snapshot cannot be date-repriced through dispatch. The server rejects the change with **A signed or tariff-rated move cannot be date-repriced here. Create an intentional quote revision first.**
- Do not attempt repeated drops or confirmations to bypass this lock. Preserve the signed/tariff record and have an authorized owner create the intentional quote revision before changing the date.
- An unsigned, non-tariff-rated move can be date-repriced by a successful dispatch save; the saved job/estimate totals are updated using the configured pricing for the new date. The system does not silently reprice a frozen signed or tariff-rated move.

> **Operational rule:** use **Dispatch** for daily job/resource assignment, **Resource availability** for durable blocks, **Fleet & crew** for resource records, **Calendar** for the older date-oriented view, and **Trip planning** for multi-day grouping of already booked jobs. Always treat server validation and visible success/error notices as final.

### Next workflow

After dispatch, assigned crew follow the controlled move-day sequence in [Crew On-Site Workspace (Field & Drivers)](#4-crew-on-site-workspace-field--drivers). For invoice, payment-record, payroll, expense, and claim follow-up, see [Billing, Payroll, Expenses & Claims](#6-billing-payroll-expenses--claims).
## 4. Crew On-Site Workspace (Field & Drivers)

<!-- help:field-checklist:start -->
### Field crew fast checklist

1. Open /app/field and select the active move.
2. Save Pre-Move Walkthrough and damage photos.
3. Tap Clock In at job arrival.
4. Save Post-Move Walkthrough, tap Clock Out, and verify calculated hours and invoice.
5. Capture the customer signature and launch checkout.

> **Use the shared job clock, not the Individual clock used for payroll.** Save required walkthroughs before clock actions. Checkout needs a finalized invoice and a configured gateway; opening checkout or returning to the app is not payment confirmation. Verify the saved payment state.
<!-- help:field-checklist:end -->

### Purpose and prerequisites

Use **Field crew** for the responsive move-day job sheet at `/app/field`. It is the field execution view for customer details, pickup and delivery information, walkthrough evidence, time capture, final billing, payment handoff, and completion.

Before a crew member can work a sheet:

1. An administrator, office administrator, or dispatcher must create/book the job and assign the crew member. The crew member must have an **active** crew record linked to the signed-in team account. The link is managed from **Fleet & crew**; the crew record's **Linked signed-in team member** field is what makes that person's assigned jobs appear in Field crew.
2. The crew member must sign in with that linked account. A **crew** user sees only jobs assigned to that linked crew profile. **Admin**, **Office Admin**, and **Dispatcher** users can use the field workflow for the jobs their role is allowed to access; this does not make an unassigned crew account able to open another job.
3. Use the workspace language selector at the top right to choose **English** or **Русский**. This chapter is in English; choose **English** when matching the labels below.
4. A phone or browser with a network connection is required. This is a responsive web workspace, not an offline/native crew app. Do not assume a disconnected device can save notes, photos, clocks, signatures, or payment state.

### Open a job sheet and check the move details

1. In the sidebar, select **Moving operations → Field crew**. The exact route is `/app/field`.
2. If more than one assigned sheet is available, select the job's date and title in the field selector. If none is available, the page shows **No assigned move sheets**; do not create a test record from the field view. Ask an authorized office user to confirm the crew link and assignment.
3. Confirm the sheet's status, customer name, scheduled date and start time, **Pickup**, **Delivery**, and **Scheduled service window**.
4. Review **Customer**. The saved phone number is available through **Call customer** and the saved email through **Email customer**. These buttons open the device's telephone or mail handler; they do not edit the customer record. If neither exists, the sheet says **No customer call or email contact is saved.**
5. Review **Pickup access notes** and **Delivery access notes** before arrival. These are the job's saved origin/destination notes; the field sheet is for reading them, not replacing the office job setup.
6. Follow the on-screen **Move-day workflow**: **Pre-move walkthrough**, **Clock in**, **Post-move walkthrough**, **Clock out**, and **Customer completion**.

> **Assignment and access limit:** The field page is not a general job search or an assignment editor. Use **Dispatch** or **Fleet & crew** (according to role) to correct assignment or crew setup. The illustrative label “+Assign Crew” is not used here unless it appears in your current authorized view.

### Record the pre-move condition (required before job clock-in)

1. In **Walkthrough & damage notes**, set **Walkthrough phase** to **Pre-move**.
2. In **Damage or condition note**, describe visible pre-existing condition clearly. The note is required when using **Save walkthrough note**. Include the item/location and condition rather than a vague statement.
3. Optionally choose an image in **Optional photo**. The field accepts image files; the server validates PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP data and limits the uploaded image to 5 MB.
4. Select **Save walkthrough note**. The saved item appears in the walkthrough list with its phase and, if supplied, a **View photo** link.
5. If no damage is present, select **No damage observed — confirm walkthrough**. This saves the phase-specific confirmation text and counts as the walkthrough. It is not a deletion or a legal certification.

The **Clock in** button remains disabled until a saved pre-move walkthrough exists. A server-side check enforces the same rule, so bypassing the disabled button is not a supported procedure.

### Clock the shared customer-billable job labor

1. After saving the pre-move walkthrough, select **Clock in**. Success is shown as **Clock-in saved. Complete the post-move walkthrough before clocking out.** The job's arrival timestamp is saved and the system emits the crew-arrival event for configured business messaging; this page does not prove that a provider is active.
2. Perform the move and record the post-move condition. Change **Walkthrough phase** to **Post-move**, write a **Damage or condition note**, optionally attach a photo, and select **Save walkthrough note** or **No damage observed — confirm walkthrough**.
3. A post-move walkthrough is required before **Clock out**. A post-move note cannot be saved through the normal field flow before the job has been clocked in.
4. When the move is finished and the post-move walkthrough is saved, select **Clock out**. Success is shown as **Clock-out saved; the server calculated the final invoice.** The shared job clock records actual labor duration, saves **Actual hours**, calculates **Final total**, and sets **Invoice status** to **unpaid**.
5. The server rejects a second clock-in, a clock-out without clock-in, a second clock-out, and an invalid elapsed time over 48 hours. If one of these occurs, stop and ask an authorized manager to review the job rather than trying to create another transition.

> **Two clocks, two purposes:** **Clock in / Clock out** is the shared, customer-billable job clock. It is not an individual payroll punch. The final invoice uses the actual job-clock duration (subject to the configured minimum/pricing rules, weekend adjustment, tariffs where configured, travel/other fees, and the job's pricing mode).

### Record individual payroll time

1. On an eligible assigned job sheet, review **Individual clock**. It is visible only to an eligible linked active crew member.
2. Select **Start individual clock** when beginning that person's payroll time. Individual clocks can start only when the assigned job is **booked** or **in progress**.
3. A crew member can have only one active individual clock at a time. If the panel says **An individual clock is active on another job. Stop it there before starting a new one.**, select that job and stop the existing timer first.
4. When the person's payroll time ends, select **Stop individual clock**. The panel refreshes and the history table records **Started**, **Stopped**, and **Payroll status**. A stopped entry is shown as **Pending review** until its timecard is reviewed; this is separate from invoice payment.
5. If the user has no active linked crew profile or is not assigned to the job, the individual clock is unavailable. Do not use the shared **Clock out** as a substitute for payroll clock-out, or vice versa.

### Review walkthrough history and linked tools

The walkthrough list keeps pre- and post-move notes and any saved photo. Use **View photo** to open a saved image. For a printable preexisting job document, use **Job documents** or the job's bill-of-lading route `/app/jobs/:id/bol` (sidebar route context: **Job documents**; the document title is **Bill of lading**). Select the existing **Job** when prompted, then review the **Customer**, **Move details**, **Inventory**, **Condition and damage notes**, **Terms and notes**, **Customer signature**, and **Completion signature**. Select **Refresh** to reload the authorized record or **Print** to print it.

The bill of lading is a generated record for recordkeeping. It states that it is not legal certification and does not replace required local documents. It can show “No damage entries are saved for this job” or “No inventory is saved for this job”; those messages mean the source record is empty, not that a new field entry should be invented there.

### Collect customer completion authorization

1. After **Clock out**, review **Final invoice & customer completion**. Confirm the displayed **Final total**, **Recorded labor hours**, rate information, **Fees**, and **Invoice status**.
2. Present the move completion to the customer and use the **Customer signature** pad. The completion action requires an actual signature image; the **Save completion** button stays disabled until a signature is supplied.
3. Select **Save completion**. Success is shown as **Customer completion signature saved.** The job receives the completion signature and moves to completed status.
4. If the page says **Customer completion signature is saved for this job.**, do not sign or submit again. The server rejects a second completion.
5. Completion cannot be saved before job clock-out. The page instead instructs: **Clock out when the move is finished to calculate final billing, then collect the customer signature.**

> **Authorization distinction:** The completion signature is the digital completion authorization captured on the field sheet. The existing customer/proposal signature and the generated bill of lading are related records, but neither should be represented as a new completion signature.

### Open hosted Stripe checkout and verify the saved state

1. Checkout is unlocked only after **Clock out** has calculated a final invoice. Before then, the page shows **Clock out after the post-move walkthrough to calculate the final invoice and unlock checkout.**
2. In **Final invoice & customer completion**, confirm the amount and select **Open Stripe checkout**. The hosted checkout opens in a new tab. It is marked **Stripe TEST** in the current field UI.
3. Tell the customer that opening the hosted page is not the same as payment confirmation. The page reports **Stripe TEST checkout opened in a new tab. Payment remains pending until a saved payment record is updated.** It checks the saved payment status periodically; a return URL or a browser tab alone does not prove payment.
4. When the saved payment record is verified as paid, the sheet shows **Payment recorded** and the invoice status becomes **paid**. Use **Billing & payments** or **Move invoices** for authorized back-office review when needed.
5. Checkout is blocked when the final invoice is missing, already paid, below the minimum checkout amount of $0.50, or when the merchant gateway is inactive. If the system reports **Stripe is inactive**, an administrator must configure the managed payment setup; do not claim that a live provider or live card charge is available.
6. Do not create a second checkout while an existing payment is pending, being prepared, or awaiting reconciliation. The server may return the existing usable hosted session or instruct staff to wait for verified settlement. If the invoice amount has changed, finish or let the existing session expire before retrying.

> **Payment limit:** This implementation uses Stripe-hosted checkout processing when the managed gateway is configured. It does not provide an in-app card-entry screen or current card charges inside the CRM. A **Stripe TEST** label and an opened checkout are not proof of a live charge.

### Completion checklist and safe troubleshooting

1. Customer and pickup/delivery details reviewed; use **Call customer** or **Email customer** only when the saved contact exists.
2. **Pre-move** walkthrough saved, with a clear note or **No damage observed — confirm walkthrough**, before **Clock in**.
3. Shared job **Clock in** saved at arrival.
4. **Post-move** walkthrough saved before **Clock out**.
5. Individual **Start individual clock / Stop individual clock** handled separately for payroll time.
6. Shared job **Clock out** saved; final invoice and actual hours displayed.
7. Customer signature captured with **Save completion**.
8. Hosted checkout opened only if needed, and **Payment recorded** or the saved invoice status is verified before describing payment as complete.
9. If a control is unavailable, read the adjacent helper text and preserve the record. Do not bypass role checks, invent a photo/signature, duplicate a clock, claim offline operation, or treat an open checkout/return URL as paid.

### Exact routes and role-aware navigation

- `/app/field` — sidebar **Moving operations → Field crew**; field job sheets and move-day workflow.
- `/app/jobs` and `/app/jobs/:id` — sidebar **Jobs**; authorized job records and setup context.
- `/app/jobs/:id/bol` — generated **Bill of lading** for an existing authorized job.
- `/app/documents` — sidebar **Job documents**; linked document tools.
- `/app/invoices` — sidebar **Move invoices**; final invoice and checkout review for authorized management roles.
- `/app/billing` — sidebar **Billing & payments**; back-office payment review for authorized finance roles.
- `/app/payroll` — sidebar **Payroll & tips**; payroll review for authorized finance roles.
- `/app/fleet` — sidebar **Fleet & crew**; crew records, active status, and linked signed-in members.
- `/app/dispatch` — sidebar **Dispatch**; management dispatch and assignment context.

The current navigation labels are authoritative. In particular, the related administration/finance routes are **Merchant gateway** (`/app/payment-gateway`), **Transactional messaging** (`/app/transactional-messages`), and **Claims & settlements** (`/app/claim-settlements`). Do not substitute stale shorthand paths or assume those providers are active merely because the route exists.

### Next workflow

For final invoice review, ledger records, payroll review, or a customer claim, use [Billing, Payroll, Expenses & Claims](#6-billing-payroll-expenses--claims). If the move includes storage, follow [Storage, Vaults & SIT Management](#5-storage-vaults--sit-management).
## 5. Storage, Vaults & SIT Management

This chapter covers MoveFlew storage records, warehouse handling, and storage-account billing.

### Access and language

- Open **Storage** at `/app/storage` from **Moving operations**.
- Open **Warehouse scanner** at `/app/scanner` from **Moving operations**.
- Storage records are available to **Admin**, **Office admin**, and **Dispatcher** roles.
- Scanner records and physical warehouse actions are limited to **Admin**, **Office admin**, and **Dispatcher** roles.
- Storage billing is in **Billing & payments** at `/app/billing`, and is limited to **Admin** and **Office admin** roles.
- 
> **Prerequisite:** Use the correct workspace before creating anything. A customer must exist before a storage agreement can be created; a warehouse must exist before a vault can be created; an agreement and a vault must exist before stored inventory can be added.

### 1. Create and maintain warehouses (facilities)

1. Go to **Storage** and open the **Warehouses** tab.
2. Select **Add warehouse**. To change an existing facility, use its **Edit** control.
3. Enter the required **Name** and **Address**. **Notes** are optional.
4. Select **Save warehouse**. The form closes, the list refreshes, and the success message is **Warehouse saved.** (or **Warehouse updated.**).

A warehouse is the physical facility record used by vaults. The **Warehouses** list shows **Name**, **Address**, and **Notes**. There is no delete control in this screen; edit the record when its details change.

### 2. Configure vaults, capacity, and status

1. Open the **Vaults** tab and select **Add vault**. The button is disabled until at least one warehouse exists.
2. Choose a **Facility** and enter the required **Name**.
3. Choose **Kind**: `vault`, `container`, or `shelf`.
4. Enter **Capacity (cu ft)**. It must be greater than zero.
5. Set **Status** to `active` or `unavailable`, then select **Save vault**.
6. Confirm the success message **Vault saved.** (or **Vault updated.**).

The vault list shows **Capacity** as occupied versus total cubic feet and a **Status** chip. Occupied cubic feet is calculated from stored inventory as quantity × cubic feet per unit; it is not a value typed into the vault form.

> **Capacity constraint:** New intake is rejected if the resulting occupied cubic feet would exceed capacity. A vault capacity cannot be edited below its current occupied amount. An `unavailable` vault cannot receive new intake or cross-dock transfers.

### 3. Create SIT or long-term storage agreements

1. Open the **Accounts** tab under **Storage** and select **New agreement**. The button requires at least one existing customer.
2. Select the **Customer**.
3. Set **Agreement kind** to `SIT` (short-term storage in transit) or `long_term`.
4. Enter the required **Start date**. **End date** is optional; leave it blank for no end date.
5. Enter **Monthly rate (USD)** with no more than two decimal places.
6. Enter **Due day** from 1 through 28.
7. Set **Status** to `active` or `closed`.
8. Optionally select **Generate monthly invoices automatically** and add **Notes**.
9. Select **Save agreement**. The success message is **Storage agreement saved.** (or **Storage agreement updated.**).

The **Customer storage accounts** list shows the customer, agreement kind, rate, dates, invoicing mode, and status. If automatic invoicing is off, it displays **Manual invoicing**. If it is on, it displays **Invoice generation enabled**.

> **Billing prerequisite:** Only an `active` agreement with **Generate monthly invoices automatically** enabled is eligible for the storage billing run. A closed agreement cannot receive a storage intake. The end date cannot be before the start date.

> **Important limit:** The agreement form does not take a payment and does not collect automatically. The application explicitly says invoice generation only creates eligible invoices; customer consent and a configured payment setup are separate owner tasks.

### 4. Intake stored inventory and assign a vault

1. Open **Inventory** and select **Add stored item**. This is enabled only when at least one storage account and one vault exist.
2. Select the **Storage account** and **Vault**.
3. Enter the required **Item name**.
4. Enter **Quantity** as a whole number of at least 1.
5. Enter **Cubic feet per unit** and **Weight (lb) per unit**. Both may be zero but cannot be negative; decimal values are supported.
6. Add optional **Notes**, then select **Save item**.
7. Confirm **Stored item saved.** and check the refreshed inventory row and **Movement timeline**.

The inventory table shows **Item**, **Account**, **Vault**, **Per unit**, **Quantity**, and **Status**. Cubic feet and weight are stored per unit; capacity uses quantity × cubic feet per unit. Saving intake creates the stored item and an `intake` movement in the timeline.

The account filter defaults to **All accounts**. Choose a customer account to show only its items and movements. The timeline records actual saved movement events; it is not a planning list.

> **Safety checks:** Intake is rejected for a closed account, an inactive vault, a record from another workspace, or insufficient vault capacity. Do not pre-multiply the per-unit measurements when entering them.

### 5. Release part or all of an item

1. In **Inventory**, find a row with quantity greater than zero and select **Release**.
2. In **Release stored item**, review **Available quantity**.
3. Enter **Quantity to release** from 1 through the available quantity.
4. Optionally add **Release notes**.
5. Select **Record release**.
6. Confirm **Release recorded.** and review the refreshed quantity, status, and **Movement timeline**.

A partial release reduces the stored quantity and leaves status `stored`. Releasing the full quantity changes the item status to `released`. The release movement is recorded with a negative quantity in the timeline.

> **Not supported here:** The Storage inventory form has no move-to-another-vault control. Do not simulate a move by releasing and manually adding a replacement item; use **Warehouse scanner** → **Cross-dock** for a physical move so source, destination, capacity, and audit records remain linked.

### 6. Run monthly storage billing

1. Open **Billing & payments** and select the **Storage billing run** tab.
2. Review the **Billing period** month. The control defaults to the current UTC month.
3. Select **Generate invoices**.
4. Wait for the success message **Storage billing run completed.**
5. Review the summary values **Created**, **Skipped**, and **Period**, then open **Invoices** to verify generated storage invoices.

The button performs a write operation; it is not a quotation. It creates one invoice per eligible active, auto-invoice storage agreement for the selected month and reports how many were created or skipped. Future periods are rejected. The server uses a storage account + month key, locks the account during generation, and treats a repeated run for the same period as already handled, so retrying does not create a second invoice for the same account and month.

#### Actual-unit proration rule

- The server counts inclusive UTC calendar days where the agreement overlaps the selected month.
- The invoice amount is `round(monthly rate in cents × overlapping days ÷ days in month)`.
- A start date in the month bills from that start date through month end.
- An end date in the month bills through that end date.
- A full-month agreement bills the full monthly rate.
- Agreements with no overlap are skipped.

> **Preview limitation:** There is no separate preview or dry-run button in this implementation. **Generate invoices** creates invoices immediately. For a review-only check, inspect the agreement dates, rate, status, and auto-invoice setting first; do not click the generate button until the owner approves the period.

> **Provider limitation:** This run creates invoice records only. It does not create a Checkout session, charge a card, or prove customer collection. If payment configuration is needed, owners configure it later in **Merchant gateway** at `/app/payment-gateway`; do not claim that a provider is active based on a generated invoice.

### 7. Create and print warehouse labels

1. Open **Warehouse scanner**.
2. In **Generate a QR label**, choose a **Saved record**. Eligible records are active `vault` or `container` locations and individual stored items; shelves are not offered as scanner targets.
3. Select **Create / show label**.
4. Wait for the QR image and opaque code to appear, then select **Print label**.

The label value is a tenant-scoped opaque local identifier; it is not a public URL. Creating or printing a label does not change inventory. If a label already exists for that record, the screen returns the existing label rather than creating a duplicate.

### 8. Resolve a label with camera or manual input

1. In **Scan a local label**, select **Start camera**. Camera scanning needs an HTTPS page, browser camera support, and permission.
2. Point the camera at the QR/barcode. The browser first uses native **BarcodeDetector** when a supported format is available (`qr_code`, `ean_13`, or `code_128`); otherwise it falls back to the ZXing browser reader.
3. If camera scanning is unavailable, enter or paste the code in **Manual label value** and select **Resolve label**.
4. After a successful resolve, the screen reports either **Item selected: …** or **Destination selected: …**. Choose the action and explicitly confirm it in the form below.

An unknown, inactive, stale, malformed, or cross-workspace value does not change storage state. It is rejected or reported as not active and appears in **Recent scanner audit** as applicable.

Select **Stop camera** when finished. The page also stops the camera when the page becomes hidden or is unmounted, clears the video stream tracks, and removes the video source. If permission is denied, no camera is found, or another application is using the camera, use manual input or saved selectors instead.

### 9. Confirm check-in, check-out, or cross-dock

1. In **Explicit storage action**, choose **Action**:
   - **Check in / intake**: re-checks in a fully released item.
   - **Check out / release**: releases part or all of a currently stored item.
   - **Cross-dock**: moves stored quantity to a different vault or container.
2. Select or scan the **Item**.
3. For intake or cross-dock, select or scan **Destination vault or container**. Only active vaults and containers with capacity are offered.
4. Enter a whole-number **Quantity** of at least 1. Add an optional **Movement note (optional)** (up to 5,000 characters).
5. Select **Confirm physical action** and wait for **Confirming…** to finish.
6. Confirm the success notice, such as **Confirmed check in / intake for …**, **Confirmed check out / release for …**, or **Confirmed cross dock for …**. Refresh or review **Recent scanner audit** and storage inventory as needed.

A scan or label resolve only selects a record; it never checks an item in, out, or across a dock. Only **Confirm physical action** records the movement. The server rechecks workspace ownership, account status, item status, quantity, destination status, and capacity at confirmation time.

- **Intake:** only an item with status `released` and quantity 0 can be checked in again; its account must be active. The destination must be active and fit the new quantity.
- **Release:** quantity cannot exceed what is currently stored. A full release leaves status `released`; a partial release leaves it `stored`.
- **Cross-dock:** quantity cannot exceed what is stored; the destination must differ from the current vault and have room. A full move changes the item’s vault; a partial move splits the quantity into a new stored item at the destination.

> **Retry and duplicate protection:** Each confirmation uses a client-generated idempotency key. Retrying the same confirmed action returns the earlier result without a second movement. Reusing the same key for different action details is rejected. If a request times out, retry the same action rather than changing the quantity or destination; the success notice may say the earlier confirmed action was returned without a second movement.

### 10. Use the scanner audit as the operational record

**Recent scanner audit** shows the latest camera/manual events with **Event**, **Target**, **Quantity**, and **Time**. Resolutions, rejected values, and confirmed physical actions are recorded separately. Use the audit and the Storage **Movement timeline** together: the audit explains label handling and confirmation, while the movement timeline shows the resulting storage movement.

> **Do not bypass confirmation:** Printing, scanning, resolving, selecting, or refreshing is non-mutating. Only the explicit save/release/generate/confirm buttons described above write the corresponding record.
