Storage invoices are created and reviewed through the finance ledger; continue with [Billing, Payroll, Expenses & Claims](#6-billing-payroll-expenses--claims). Use [Reports, Marketing & Webhooks](#7-reports-marketing--webhooks) for record-based reporting and owner-controlled automation.
## 6. Billing, Payroll, Expenses & Claims

### Who can use this chapter

The finance workspace pages are available to **Admin** and **Office admin** roles. **Dispatcher**, **Estimator**, and **Crew** do not receive these finance controls. Merchant payment policy changes and refund reconciliation require **Admin**; payment controls otherwise require an administrator. QuickBooks accounting and claim settlements are restricted to **Admin** and **Office admin**. The public customer claim page is reached through a scoped link, not through staff navigation.

**Navigation authority:** use the sidebar labels **Move invoices**, **Billing & payments**, **Expenses**, **Payroll & tips**, **Claims**, **Merchant gateway**, **QuickBooks accounting**, and **Claims & settlements**. The real routes are `/app/invoices`, `/app/billing`, `/app/expenses`, `/app/payroll`, `/app/claims`, `/app/payment-gateway`, `/app/accounting`, and `/app/claim-settlements`.

### 1. Keep Move invoices separate from Billing & payments

**Move invoices** is the original job-invoice area. **Billing & payments** is the audited operations ledger for new invoices, balances, recorded payments, and storage billing. Its invoice list explicitly does not migrate legacy records automatically. Do not describe a Billing record as a replacement for the original job invoice.

1. Open **Billing & payments** and choose **New invoice**. A customer must exist first; the button is disabled when there are no customers.
2. In **New invoice**, select **Customer**. **Related job** is optional and only shows that customer’s jobs. Select **Invoice kind**: `manual` or `deposit`. The implemented form does not offer `tip` as a create choice, although the ledger supports the `tip` kind for records created elsewhere.
3. Enter the required **Due date**. Under **Line items**, enter a **Description**, whole-number **Quantity**, and **Unit price (USD)**. Use **Add line** for additional items; there must be at least one line. **Notes** is optional.
4. Choose **Save invoice**. On success the list refreshes and shows **Invoice saved.** Values are converted to integer cents; dollar input may have no more than two decimals. The server calculates the total from quantity × unit cents (up to 100 lines).
5. Use the row’s **Edit** control to change **Due date** or **Notes**, then choose **Save changes**. The success state is **Invoice updated.** Use **Void invoice** only when the invoice has no recorded payment. A void invoice cannot be changed or receive payment; the success state is **Invoice voided.**
6. Read the columns **Total**, **Paid**, **Balance**, and **Status**. Status is derived as `open`, `partial`, `paid`, or `void`; it is not a free-form label. A partial payment leaves the remaining balance.

**Tip:** storage is not a manual invoice type. In **Billing & payments** > **Storage billing run**, select **Billing period** and choose **Generate invoices**. The result shows **Created**, **Skipped**, and **Period**. This action creates eligible active auto-invoice agreements once per period; it never charges a customer.

### 2. Record a payment without pretending to process a card

1. In an invoice row with a positive balance, choose **Record payment**.
2. Confirm the displayed **Open balance**. Enter a positive **Amount (USD)** no greater than that balance, choose **Method** (`cash`, `check`, `external_card`, or `other`), and enter the required **Reference**.
3. Choose **Record payment**. The success state is **Payment record saved.** The invoice’s **Paid**, **Balance**, and status refresh; an exact-balance entry becomes `paid`, and a smaller entry becomes `partial`.

This is a manual accounting record only. It does not process a card and does not store card details. The server records integer cents, rejects overpayment and payments to void/paid invoices, and uses an operation key to prevent accidental duplicate posting. The **Payment ledger** tab displays date, invoice, method, reference, and amount.

For a hosted test checkout, use the row’s **Stripe TEST** button. A new browser window opens and the success notice says **Stripe TEST checkout opened. The verified ledger will refresh when you return; payment is not assumed.** Do not mark an invoice paid based on the window alone; trust only the refreshed verified ledger.

### 3. Merchant gateway: consent, holds, and owner activation

Open **Merchant gateway**. Provider setup is owner-controlled and may be configured later. Do not enter card or bank details into CRM, and do not claim that a provider is active from the presence of these controls.

#### Create customer consent

1. In **Request customer authorization**, choose **Customer** and choose **Method**: **Card for future holds** or **ACH bank account**.
2. Review or edit **Agreement shown to customer**.
3. Choose **Create secure customer link**. The success notice is **Customer link created. Their consent is still required.** Use **Open customer authorization page** or **Copy link**. The customer accepts the terms before redirection to the hosted provider page.

#### Configure the merchant policy (Admin)

An Admin may review **Provider state**, **Business timezone**, **Hours before move (24–48)**, and **Estimate buffer (%)**, plus the switches **Enable live collection**, **Offer Stripe-verified ACH bank debit**, and **Enable scheduled consented card holds**. Choose **Save policy** only after review. Its confirmation is **Policy saved. No funds were held by saving it.** Saving policy is not a charge or hold.

Owner activation is separate: live collection requires the owner’s live keys in project Integrations, republishing, and the workspace live switch. Treat the displayed provider state as the implementation’s current state, not proof that an active provider is available.

#### Prepare and finish a card hold

1. In **Schedule an estimated hold**, choose a booked **Booked move** and that customer’s **Customer’s active card consent**.
2. Choose **Prepare scheduled hold**. The confirmation says **Scheduled. The native runner must be separately enabled.** This prepares the record; it does not itself prove that a hold was placed.
3. The policy is designed for a **24–48 hour** pre-move window and a **15% estimate buffer** (review the displayed owner policy before relying on it). A card hold is authorization, not revenue or a payment ledger entry.
4. In **Authorization history**, read **Requested / held / captured**, **State**, and **Hold / expiry**. For a held or capture-due row, choose **Capture invoice** only after confirming the finalized invoice amount. The confirmation is **Capture submitted. Verified evidence controls the ledger.** Choose **Release hold** when the authorization should be released; the confirmation is **Release submitted.**
5. Capture and release are separate owner/provider actions. Never treat preparation, a browser redirect, or a scheduled state as captured funds.

**ACH constraint:** ACH is a debit, not a preauthorization, and does not create a card hold. Do not promise the 24–48 hour hold behavior for ACH.

**Refund constraint:** the managed webhook does not subscribe to `charge.refunded`. In **Saved agreements & refunds**, only an Admin should choose **Reconcile actual Stripe refunds**. The success notice is **Verified Stripe refund reconciliation finished.** This is reconciliation of verified provider evidence, not a manual refund button.

### 4. QuickBooks accounting: map, review, then send

Open **QuickBooks accounting**. Connection, credentials, provider activation, and the separate owner enablement for inbound and outbound are configured later by the owner. If inactive, the page states that no connection, sync, or accounting write is enabled.

1. Review **Connection**, **Reconciliation safeguards**, and **Required account mappings**. Account IDs must come from the linked QuickBooks company; an account name is not an ID. Missing or inactive mappings leave journals awaiting mapping.
2. Review **Local journal review queue**. Candidates can come from legacy jobs/payments, operations invoices and ledger entries, supported expenses, tips, and append-only claim accounting lines. Amounts are integer cents and journals must balance.
3. For a `queued_review` or `send_failed` row, choose **Approve for sending** only after checking source, date, memo, amount, and mappings. Approval is not a provider send.
4. For an approved row, choose **Send to QuickBooks** as a second, deliberate action. The success notice comes from the reviewed action; refresh and verify the resulting state. An uncertain send is not resent.
5. For an `uncertain` row, choose **Read back only**. This checks the stored request outcome; it does not send again.
6. In **Inbound QuickBooks reconciliation**, inspect the QuickBooks entity, local candidate, both amounts, decision, and reason. Choose **Apply safe update** only for a pending invoice/payment with a safe local match.

**Important limit:** inbound application never changes local money or marks an invoice paid. A remote journal entry is shown as **Unsupported locally**; other unsafe matches require **Manual reconciliation required**. Do not use QuickBooks as a shortcut around the local approval and payment-ledger workflow.

### 5. Record operating expenses

1. Open **Expenses** and choose **Add expense**.
2. In **Add expense**, optionally select **Related job** or leave **No related job**. Enter required **Category**, **Amount (USD)**, **Incurred date**, and **Vendor**. **Notes** is optional.
3. Choose **Save expense**. The register refreshes with **Expense saved.** Amounts are stored as integer cents and displayed in the selected locale.

Use **Cancel** to discard the form. Amounts must be valid, non-negative dollar values with no more than two decimals. This register is for actual expense records, not revenue or cash collection. QuickBooks only auto-sources approved categories; an unsupported category is left for manual mapping.

### 6. Payroll and tips are review/export records, not disbursement

#### Timecards

1. Open **Payroll & tips** > **Timecards** and choose **Add timecard**. A crew member must exist.
2. Select **Crew member**; optionally select **Related job**. Enter **Work date**, whole non-negative **Worked minutes**, whole non-negative **Break minutes**, and **Hourly rate (USD)**. **Notes** is optional.
3. An Admin may select **Admin approval**. Non-Admin users cannot set that checkbox; their saved timecard remains unapproved.
4. Choose **Save timecard**. The success state is **Timecard saved.** Editing uses **Edit timecard** and returns **Timecard updated.**

Timecards are separate from customer-billed job time. They are the source for review totals only.

#### Weekly review and CSV

1. Choose **Weekly review** and set **Week starting**. The report runs through the displayed end date.
2. Verify **Regular**, **Overtime**, **Rate**, **Regular pay**, **Overtime pay**, **Tips**, and **Total**. The server applies the 40-hour calendar-week and 1.5× overtime review rules to actual approved data.
3. Choose **Export CSV** for a file with crew, minutes, rates, regular/overtime pay, tips, and total. **Print** prints the review.

The page explicitly does not perform tax withholding, employment classification, or payroll disbursement. There is no actual payroll payment action here.

#### Manual tip allocation

1. Choose **Tips** > **Allocate tip**. The button is available only when a job has assigned crew.
2. In **Allocate manual tip**, choose **Job**, enter **Tip amount (USD)** and **Method**, then enter an amount for each **Assigned crew allocation** member.
3. The allocations must equal the tip amount exactly, in integer cents. Choose **Save allocation**; the success state is **Tip allocation saved.**

This is a record-only manual allocation. It does not distribute money. A digital tip invoice is allocated only after independently verified payment.

### 7. Base Claims: create, update, and note a claim

Open **Claims** for the base claim register. A saved job is required; **New claim** is disabled when no jobs exist.

1. Choose **New claim**. Select **Linked job**, then enter required **Claim type**, **Claimed amount (USD)**, and **Description**. **Response due date** is optional.
2. Choose **Save claim**. The register refreshes with **Claim saved.** Claimed and approved amounts are stored as integer cents.
3. Use **Edit claim** to open **Claim detail**. Review **Status**, **Approved amount (USD)**, **Due date**, and **Resolution**, then choose **Save claim changes**. The success state is **Claim updated.** The available status values come from the implementation’s claim-status list.
4. Choose **Load notes** to load the **Staff note timeline**. Enter **Internal note** and choose **Add note**. The success state is **Claim note saved.** Notes are durable internal claim events.

**Limit:** a claim status, approved amount, or resolution is not a refund promise. Base **Claims** does not send a payout.

### 8. Claims & settlements: post-move evidence and a manual external record

Open **Claims & settlements**. Only **Admin** and **Office admin** can manage it. The desk is manual-record-only: it does not send money, create a Stripe refund, or prove that a payment occurred.

#### Issue the customer’s post-move claim link

1. Select a claim under **Claims requiring review** and choose **Open**.
2. Under **Customer portal access**, set **Link expiration** and choose **Issue scoped link**. The link is limited to the linked completed move and can be revoked. It is not automatically sent to the customer.
3. Use **Copy now** to copy the displayed link. The token cannot be retrieved later from this screen. Use **Revoke** on an active link when access must stop.

The customer opens the link at `/claims/:token`. The portal is explicitly a **Post-move claim** page and is available only after the linked job is completed. While the claim remains editable, the customer can:

1. In **Add an affected item**, enter **Item name**, **What happened**, whole **Quantity**, and **Amount requested (USD)**, then choose **Save item**. The success notice is **Item detail saved for staff review.**
2. In **Add a photo**, optionally choose **Related item (optional)**, select a **Photo**, optionally enter **Caption (optional)**, and choose **Upload photo**. PNG, JPEG, or WebP is accepted up to 5 MB; the server verifies the file. The success notice is **Photo added to this claim.**
3. Choose **Submit claim details** when evidence is complete. The success state is **Submitted for staff review.** Submission alerts staff through the claim record; it does not issue a refund, payout, or payment instruction. Once submitted or otherwise closed, customer updates may no longer be accepted.

#### Approve or deny once

1. In **Terminal decision**, choose **Decision**: **Approve** or **Deny**.
2. For approval, enter a positive **Approved amount (USD)** and choose **Resolution**: **Cash settlement** or **Repair**. Enter an **Internal review note** as needed.
3. Choose **Approve claim** or **Deny claim**. Approval records the claim decision and liability journal; denial records the denial. No payout is sent.

A terminal decision is final in this desk: it cannot be replaced or re-approved. Review the customer, completed move, claimed amount, affected items, photos, and remaining liability before submitting.

#### Record a completed external settlement

1. Use **Record an external settlement** only after an eligible approved claim exists. The page shows **Remaining approved liability**.
2. Choose **Recorded method**: **Manual external cash payout record**, **External processor refund record**, or **Repair completed**.
3. Enter positive **Amount (USD)** no greater than the remaining approved liability and the required **External reference** (receipt, repair order, or processor reference).
4. Choose **Record completed external action**. The success notice is **External settlement record and liability-clearance journal were saved. No payout or refund was executed.** Refresh and verify **Recorded externally** and **Remaining liability**.

Partial settlements are supported: record only the amount actually completed, and the remaining approved liability stays visible for a later manual record. Never enter an unperformed payout or use an invented reference. A resolved/fully settled claim cannot accept another settlement. The **Liability and settlement audit** is append-only and shows method, amount, external reference, and claim accounting lines.

### Quick safety checklist

- Use **Move invoices** for the original job-invoice context; use **Billing & payments** for the audited operations ledger.
- Treat every dollar entry as converted to integer cents; use no more than two decimals and whole quantities/minutes where requested.
- A manual payment, hold preparation, approval, QuickBooks approval, claim submission, or settlement record is not itself proof that money moved.
- Confirm the success notice and refreshed ledger/register after each save.
- Keep owner activation, provider credentials, live capture, refunds, QuickBooks sends, and external payouts with the owner/provider process; this CRM records reviewed evidence and deliberate actions only.

## 7. Reports, Marketing & Webhooks

**Audience and access.** This chapter covers **Reports**, **Marketing**, **Reviews**, **Integrations & API**, and **Automations** in the role-aware workspace sidebar. Office roles (admin, office admin, estimator, and dispatcher) can use the reporting, campaign, and private-feedback areas. **Integrations & API** and automation configuration are restricted to **Admin** and **Office admin**. If a menu item is not visible, the selected workspace role does not have access.

The current sidebar locations are **Growth & insights > Reports**, **Growth & insights > Marketing**, **Growth & insights > Reviews**, **Administration > Integrations & API**, and **Administration > Automations**. Related owner configuration is reached through **Finance & service > Merchant gateway**, **Administration > Transactional messaging**, **Finance & service > QuickBooks accounting**, and **Finance & service > Claims & settlements**. The direct routes are `/app/payment-gateway`, `/app/transactional-messages`, and `/app/claim-settlements`.

### Reports: filter the period and export actual rows

1. Open **Reports**. The page initially loads the current month. The page caption explains that revenue, costs, and attribution are calculated from actual workspace records.
2. Set **From** and **To** using the date controls. Click **Apply dates**. The button reloads the report for the applied range; changing a date without applying it does not change the figures.
3. Read the KPI cards: **Leads**, **Booked**, **Completed**, **Estimated revenue**, **Collected revenue**, **Recorded expenses**, and **Net contribution**. Estimated revenue comes from saved estimate totals; collected revenue is recorded collections only; expenses are expense records in the selected period.
4. Treat **Net contribution** as an operational estimate, not audited profit. It is based on recorded revenue and expenses and excludes unmodeled costs; it is not a tax or financial-statement figure. The page also states that manual operational invoice-ledger collections are kept separate where there is no durable cross-ledger deduplication key.
5. Use **Funnel** for counts by saved customer stage and **Revenue by month** for booked versus collected values. An empty period shows an empty-state message rather than invented totals.
6. Use **Source attribution** to compare saved lead source with **Leads**, **Booked**, **Collected revenue**, **Spend**, **Cost per lead**, and **ROAS**. ROAS and source ROI are approximations from saved CRM attribution and recorded campaign spend, not imported advertising-network results. Missing denominators display as `—`.
7. Click **Export actual records** to download a CSV named for the applied date range. It exports the record-level rows returned by the reporting API. The button is disabled when no rows are returned; it does not export a synthetic KPI summary.

**Conversion and ROI limit.** There is no separate “sales conversion” KPI or third-party channel report in this implementation. Use the displayed funnel counts and the source table’s Leads/Booked relationship as an operational conversion approximation. Use ROAS (collected revenue divided by recorded spend where available) as an approximate source return measure only.

### Marketing: record campaigns and UTM/source context

1. Open **Marketing** and confirm that you have an office role. Users without permission see a permission notice and cannot add or edit campaigns.
2. Click **Add campaign**. Complete the required fields **Campaign name**, **Source**, **Start date**, **End date**, and **Spend (cents)**. **Notes** is optional.
3. Enter spend as a non-negative integer number of cents: for example, `12500` represents `$125.00`. The end date must be on or after the start date. Save with **Save campaign**; a successful save closes the dialog and refreshes the **Campaign log**.
4. Review the log’s **Campaign**, **Source**, **Period**, **Spend**, and **Notes** columns. Use **Edit** to revise an existing record and then **Save campaign**. Campaign records are workspace data used by the report calculations; they are not proof of ad-platform spend.
5. Use **Current source metrics** to see current-month saved lead and campaign data. The implementation does not import ad-network reporting.
6. For incoming web/portal/API attribution, preserve the available UTM fields (source, medium, campaign, content, keyword, ad group, or custom tracking) in the originating intake or integration. The CRM validates and stores these values for attribution; it does not claim that an ad network received or verified them.
7. Review **Follow-up sequences** on this page for sequence name, channel, trigger, and enabled/delivery status. Click **Open sequence editor in Settings** to edit sequences. **Run eligible follow-ups** evaluates eligible rules and reports success when they were evaluated; it does not mean an email or SMS was delivered.

**Marketing delivery limit.** The campaign log stores source, dates, spend, and notes only. No ad-platform, social posting, email, or SMS delivery is implied. Configure owners, templates, consent, and a real provider in **Transactional messaging** before treating a follow-up as deliverable.

### Reviews: create a neutral private feedback link

1. Open **Reviews** and click **Create feedback request**. This is available to office roles.
2. In **Customer**, choose a saved customer. This is required. **Related job (optional)** is filtered to jobs belonging to that customer; leave **No related job** when no job should be associated.
3. Click **Create private link**. A successful result opens **Private feedback link created** and displays the one-time link.
4. Immediately use **Copy link**, then click **Done**. The token is not shown again after the dialog closes. Share it only through your approved process.
5. Review the **Feedback requests** table for **Customer**, **Status**, **Rating**, **Feedback**, **Created**, and **Public review link**. Returned private responses can show a 1–5 rating and feedback; an absent response displays `—`.

**Review limit.** Creating a request creates a neutral private link and queues an internal business-message record, but the workspace does not send an email, SMS, or public review request. It has no positive-rating gate and does not publish or sync to a social/review network. A link expires after the implementation’s request lifetime (90 days) and may be one-time/invalid after use. Do not describe **Copy link** as “sent.”

### Integrations & API: connections, keys, widgets, and portals

1. Open **Integrations & API** as an **Admin** or **Office admin**. The **Vendor connections** tab reports registry status only. Provider names may be listed for documentation, but a listing is not an active connection. The current implementation reports email and SMS as not connected and documents providers as not connected; do not claim an active gateway, accounting sync, marketing sync, social/review integration, or other provider.
2. Use the owner shortcuts when required: **Merchant gateway** opens `/app/payment-gateway`, **Email & SMS** opens `/app/transactional-messages`, and **QuickBooks Online** opens `/app/accounting`. Credentials and live activation are separate configuration steps.
3. In **API keys**, click **Create key**. Required fields are **Name** and at least one **Authorized scopes** selection. Choose **Kind**: `api`, `widget`, or `portal`.
   - `api` supports the least required selection from `leads:create`, `read:customers`, `read:jobs`, and `read:storage`.
   - `widget` is restricted to `leads:create` and creates an embedded quote-intake capability.
   - `portal` uses `portal:read` and optionally `portal:inventory:submit`, and requires **Bound customer**. It exposes only that customer’s portal data.
   - **Expires on (optional)** may be set to a future date/time. If omitted, the server applies a default expiry (90 days for API/widget, 30 days for portal); expiry cannot be more than 366 days away.
4. Click **Create key**. The full token appears in a one-time secret dialog. Use **Copy token** and store it in the approved secret manager; never paste it into notes, browser storage, or logs. The list later shows only name, kind, scopes, customer binding, expiry, prefix, and status—not the token.
5. Revoke a key with **Revoke**. Revocation is the supported deactivation action and is permanent for that key; create a replacement if access is needed again.
6. In **Embed forms**, an active widget key produces a one-time quote URL and iframe code. Use **Copy relative link** or **Copy iframe code** in the creation dialog. If the token is lost, create a replacement widget key; the original cannot be recovered.
7. In **Portal links**, an active portal key shows its bound customer and a browser-relative `/portal/<one-time-token>` form. Portal keys must remain customer-bound and one-time tokens are not listed after creation.
8. In **Docs**, read the safe metadata and schema returned by the built-in developer documentation. It contains no live secrets.

**REST example (placeholder only).** The actual authenticated API base is `/api/crm/engage`; versioned API-key routes are under `/api/crm/engage/v1`. Replace placeholders through an approved secret-handling process—never put a real key in this manual:

```bash
curl -X POST https://<published-origin>/api/crm/engage/v1/leads \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-api-key: PLACEHOLDER_API_KEY' \
  -d '{"name":"PLACEHOLDER_NAME","email":"placeholder@example.com","phone":"+1 555 010 0000","source":"PLACEHOLDER_SOURCE"}'
```

The API requires the `leads:create` scope and validates email, phone, and required name. The documented read routes are `/api/crm/engage/v1/customers`, `/api/crm/engage/v1/jobs`, and `/api/crm/engage/v1/storage-accounts` (with `read:customers`, `read:jobs`, and `read:storage` respectively). Use pagination (`limit` 1–100 and `offset`) as documented.

### Webhooks: sign, test, and troubleshoot without guessing

1. In **Webhooks**, click **Add webhook**. Enter an **HTTPS destination URL** and **Events (comma separated)**, then choose **Enable after creation**. Supported event names are `lead.created`, `customer.created`, `job.booked`, `job.completed`, `invoice.paid`, and `storage.updated`.
2. The destination must be a publicly routable HTTPS URL. Credentials in the URL, fragments, localhost, private/reserved addresses, and hostnames resolving to non-public addresses are rejected. Click **Create webhook** only when an external receiver is ready.
3. The signing secret appears once in **Webhook signing secret**. Copy it with **Copy token** and store it securely; it cannot be retrieved later. Deliveries include signed headers such as event, timestamp, and an HMAC SHA-256 signature.
4. Use **Enable** or **Disable** to change the target state. A disabled target will not be delivered to. Use **Send real test** only on an enabled target; it creates a real signed `webhook.test` request and reports the server attempt.
5. Read **Delivery history** for status, event, time, HTTP status, and error. Only server-recorded attempts appear there. Failed delivery attempts are retried with increasing delay up to three attempts; an endpoint returning success (HTTP 2xx) is recorded as delivered.

**Webhook safety limit.** Creating a webhook does not post anything immediately. Domain events are queued in a workspace-scoped outbox. A test is explicitly real and can contact the external HTTPS endpoint. Never use **Send real test** against a third-party destination unless the owner has approved it. “Queued,” “failed,” or “uncertain” delivery history is not proof that an external system processed the event; investigate the receiver and signature before retrying outside the CRM.

### Automations: native registration is explicit and bounded

1. Open **Automations**. Only **Admin** and **Office admin** can view/manage the configuration. Opening the page never registers or runs a task.
2. Confirm **Native scheduler**, **Workspace runner**, **Cadence**, **Current billing period**, **Last callback**, and **Published origin**. The cadence is every five minutes in UTC and the callback target is the workspace’s scheduled endpoint. A state of **Planned setup** or **Activation blocked** means no scheduler has been registered.
3. Before activation, the owner must configure the canonical published HTTPS origin and the platform scheduler/runtime prerequisites. **Activate scheduler** is enabled only when the server says the target is ready. Clicking it verifies the canonical origin and health route, requests native registration, and records the returned real task UID. If registration does not return a task UID, activation is not recorded.
4. After a successful activation, confirm the state is **Active stored configuration** and that a stored configuration shows the task status and cadence. Only the workspace member who created the scheduler can change its platform task. Use **Pause scheduler** to disable it and **Resume scheduler** to enable it again; each action updates the native task and stored workspace status. Use **Refresh** to reread status.
5. Use **Webhook targets** to open **Integrations & API** and configure approved HTTPS targets. The runner only pumps queued outbox IDs selected from this workspace and does not invent delivery history.
6. Understand the five-minute runner’s work: it generates current-period storage invoices, evaluates enabled lead sequences into duplicate-protected internal reminders, and delivers bounded signed webhook outbox items. Generating an invoice does not collect payment. A lead reminder does not itself become an email or SMS delivery.
7. The same authenticated callback also evaluates the separately gated **Merchant gateway**, **Transactional messaging**, and **QuickBooks accounting** workers. When their provider credentials and owner switches are ready, these can create due, consented card authorizations, process eligible queued messages, and run approved outbound or reviewed inbound accounting work. Scheduling alone does not enable those modules; templates, recipient consent, payment-method agreements, account mappings, and the relevant module permissions still apply.
8. Review each module’s recorded status after a callback. The runner never automatically captures a held amount and never issues a claim payout. An authorization holds funds; it is not an invoice payment. Unknown message or accounting submissions require provider reconciliation rather than an automatic second send.

**Automation limit.** This page is opt-in native scheduling, not an immediate “run now” control. Activation, pause, and resume require explicit button clicks and authenticated workspace ownership; there is no promise that a provider is active merely because a provider name appears elsewhere in the UI.

### Operating checklist

- Confirm the selected workspace and role before interpreting any page.
- Apply the report dates before comparing KPIs, and export only when **Export actual records** is enabled.
- Record campaign spend as integer cents and describe source metrics as CRM approximations.
- Create private feedback links only for saved customers; copy the token before closing the dialog and say “created,” never “sent.”
- Treat all keys and webhook secrets as one-time credentials; copy and vault them immediately.
- Use only approved public HTTPS webhook targets and regard a real test as an external post.
- Activate automation only after the owner has verified the canonical published origin and prerequisites; verify the stored task identity and state afterward.

### Next workflow

For a rejected action, uncertain integration state, time/date issue, or safe escalation checklist, see [Troubleshooting & FAQ](#8-troubleshooting--faq).
## 8. Troubleshooting & FAQ

This chapter is for staff who need to understand a warning, status, or blocked action before escalating it.

### Before you start

- Sign in to the correct workspace. Your role controls what appears in the grouped sidebar. **Admin** and **Office admin** have the broadest finance and administration access; **Dispatcher** handles dispatch and operations; **Sales & estimator** handles sales tools; **Field crew** has field access. If a page is missing, ask an owner to confirm the workspace and role before treating it as a defect.
- Use the sidebar’s actual labels: **Moving operations → Dispatch**, **Moving operations → Fleet & crew**, **Moving operations → Resource availability**, **Moving operations → Storage**, **Moving operations → Inventory catalog**, **Finance & service → Merchant gateway**, **Finance & service → QuickBooks accounting**, **Finance & service → Claims & settlements**, and **Administration → Transactional messaging**.
- Never paste card numbers, bank details, provider credentials, access tokens, or customer secrets into an escalation.

### 1. Why is an estimate accepted but still “not booked”?

**Accepted** is not the same as a booked move. An estimate can be accepted while the operational booking, schedule, crew, truck, and time block are still unresolved. Do not promise a crew or date from an accepted estimate alone.

1. Open **Estimates** and confirm the estimate’s current status and customer details.
2. Open the related job from **Jobs** (or the job link shown by the estimate) and confirm that the move is actually booked before dispatching it.
3. In **Dispatch**, check the job’s date/time block and resources. If it is not booked, resolve the missing booking step or ask an office admin/owner; do not create a duplicate job or invent an assignment.

**Limit:** There is no safe “accepted means booked” shortcut. If the interface does not show a booking action for that record, leave it unbooked and escalate with the estimate/job ID.

### 2. Why was a crew, driver, skill, truck, or capacity choice rejected?

The availability and dispatch checks are intentional. A candidate can be unavailable because the person is inactive, is not marked as a driver where driving is required, lacks a required skill, or is already committed in an overlapping date/time block. A truck can be rejected when it is inactive, unavailable, or does not meet the job’s capacity requirement.

1. Open **Fleet & crew** and verify that the member and truck are active and their capabilities are recorded.
2. Verify the job’s move date, start/end time, required skills, driver requirement, truck requirement, and capacity in **Dispatch** or **Resource availability**.
3. Correct the source record or choose another eligible resource, then reload the job before saving.
4. If a warning names a date/time overlap or insufficient capacity, do not force the assignment; change the block or select a resource that passes the guard.

**Concrete warnings to respect:** “No eligible crew,” “Mark eligible crew members as drivers in Fleet & crew,” “No truck selected,” “No truck assigned,” and capacity/overlap warnings. These are operational constraints, not suggestions.

### 3. What does a “stale write” or changed-record warning mean?

Another user (or another browser tab) saved the record after you loaded it. The server rejects an old version rather than overwriting newer data.

1. Stop clicking **Save** or retrying the same request.
2. Copy any unsaved notes to a safe internal draft, reload the record, and compare the current values.
3. Re-enter only the intended change and save once.
4. If the warning repeats, close duplicate tabs and report the record ID, action, approximate time, and the visible warning.

**Tip:** A stale-write rejection means the newer server record remains authoritative; it does not mean the earlier save partially happened.

### 4. Why do date, time, language, or currency look different?

- Date-only move dates are calendar dates; do not convert them to UTC or move them backward/forward based on your computer clock.
- Scheduled payment timing uses the workspace business timezone. A payment due “on the move date” may therefore execute according to the configured business-day clock, not your browser’s timezone.
- The top-bar language selector changes labels only. It does not translate customer-entered text or change amounts.
- Payment and accounting checks use USD/cents in the current implementation. A currency mismatch is a provider/record configuration issue, not a reason to manually retype an amount.

When escalating, include the workspace timezone, displayed date/time, browser timezone, currency shown, and record ID—never credentials.

### 5. Why is a catalog item’s custom name or label missing?

**Inventory catalog** stores the catalog name and the staff-facing custom name/label separately. A custom label does not rewrite historical job, storage, or invoice descriptions automatically.

1. Open **Inventory catalog** and find the item.
2. Confirm the saved custom name/label and any unit or quantity fields.
3. Save the catalog record, then reload the consuming page before using it.
4. For an existing job or invoice whose description is already saved, update that document through its own supported edit flow; do not assume changing the catalog retroactively changes it.

### 6. Why are there two clocks, and why is clock-out/payment blocked?

The field time record and the job’s operational timestamps are different records. A field worker’s individual clock is not automatically the job’s final clock-out. Final payment capture also has guards: the job must have a clock-out and a final total, and the payment must pass the verified ledger/webhook checks.

1. In **Field**, confirm the worker’s individual clock entries.
2. In the job record, confirm the move/job clock-out and final total are present.
3. In **Move invoices** or **Billing & payments**, check whether the invoice is merely open, paid, partially refunded, or refunded.
4. If a payment says it cannot proceed because there is no clock-out or final total, finish the authorized operational closeout first. Do not mark an invoice paid manually to bypass it.

**Important:** A completed checkout that is marked unpaid is not a paid invoice. “Paid” requires the verified payment event/ledger path, not merely a browser success page.

### 7. Why can’t an ACH payment charge, or why does it say credentials are live but charging is unavailable?

A configured-looking gateway is not proof that live charging is available. The gateway must be enabled, credentials must be valid for the selected mode, the payment method/consent must be eligible, and provider verification must succeed. ACH also follows provider-specific asynchronous states; it is not an instant card result.

1. An authorized finance user opens **Merchant gateway** and checks mode, enabled state, credential status, and the configured currency.
2. Check the customer’s payment agreement/consent and the payment attempt status in **Billing & payments**.
3. If the screen says **inactive**, **not configured**, **credentials unavailable**, or **cannot charge**, stop. Do not retry repeatedly or collect card/bank details in notes.
4. Ask the owner to configure or rotate credentials and perform the provider’s live verification. Staff should not claim a successful charge until the settled/verified status appears.

**Limit:** Development did not activate providers or perform live holds, charges, refunds, or end-to-end merchant checks. Owners selected providers must configure and verify them later.

### 8. How should I handle a refund or a fixed/refund webhook warning?

Refunds are reconciled through the central verified webhook ledger. A provider response or a manually typed note is not enough to prove the local ledger changed.

1. Open **Billing & payments** and record the payment/invoice ID and current status.
2. Check the refund record and the verified webhook/reconciliation status.
3. If the status is pending, failed, or requires reconciliation, do not issue a second refund.
4. Escalate the payment ID, refund ID (if shown), amount/currency, timestamp, and exact status text. Never include a secret key or full payment credentials.

**Limit:** The app’s safe behavior is to acknowledge a matching webhook and apply it once. A mismatched, duplicate, or stale event is not applied as money.

### 9. Why does QuickBooks say approved, but not sent—or sent, uncertain, read back, or inbound amounts not applied?

QuickBooks work has separate review and transmission states.

- **Approved** means the journal passed the local review gate; it does not mean Intuit accepted it.
- **Sent** means a provider submission was recorded, but staff should still use the stored provider/readback evidence where available.
- **Uncertain** means the outcome cannot safely be inferred. Use the read-only recovery/readback action or ask an owner to reconcile; do not resend blindly.
- Inbound changes are staged for human review. Safe mapped invoice due dates may be applied automatically, but external monetary edits, paid-state transitions, and inbound JournalEntry imports are deliberately not applied to the authoritative local ledger.

1. Open **QuickBooks accounting** and inspect the journal’s status and request identity.
2. For **uncertain**, use the available readback/recovery view and compare the provider record before any retry.
3. For inbound amounts not applied, review the staged change and update the local record through the approved workflow; never force a paid state to match an external amount.

**Limit:** Deposits remain unearned liabilities until the supported closeout recognition; do not treat an export as immediate revenue.

### 10. Why did an SMS get blocked, show STOP, or remain ambiguous?

SMS requires a valid recipient and recorded consent. A signed inbound **STOP** suppresses messaging locally; no automatic reply is sent. After STOP, a documented re-opt-in is required before transactional SMS can be enabled again.

1. Open **Communications** or **Transactional messaging** and inspect the message status.
2. **Blocked—no consent** means do not submit it. Verify the recipient and record consent through the supported consent flow, including source and channel.
3. If a customer sent STOP, do not override suppression. Obtain the documented re-opt-in first.
4. If submission says **ambiguous**, or the worker lease expired, delivery is unknown. Reconcile provider evidence before any manual retry; the system does not automatically retry an ambiguous submission.

**SES note:** SES currently provides accepted/failed/uncertain submission evidence, not verified receipt or bounce ingestion. **Accepted** is not **delivered**.

### 11. Why did a storage invoice have a strange quantity, prorated amount, or duplicate cycle?

Storage quantities and billing cycles are guarded to prevent double charging. **Invoice generation does not charge a customer**; automatic collection is not connected until consent is recorded.

1. In **Storage**, verify the agreement’s facility/vault, start date, end date, rate, due day, status, and auto-invoice setting.
2. Check quantity, cubic feet/weight where applicable, and the cycle dates. A partial first or final cycle can be prorated by the configured billing rules.
3. Search invoices for the same agreement and cycle before generating again. If a cycle already exists, do not create a duplicate.
4. If the amount is wrong, record the agreement ID, cycle dates, quantity, rate, and existing invoice ID; ask an authorized finance user to correct the source agreement or invoice.

### 12. Why did the native schedule not run?

Native scheduled work is deliberately explicit. It is registered only after an owner action, uses the platform’s returned task identity, and requires each provider’s own enabled settings and credentials.

1. Open **Automations** and confirm the automation is enabled and has an explicit owner/activation record.
2. Confirm the deployed callback/origin is configured and the relevant provider is independently enabled.
3. If configuration is incomplete, the scheduler skips that provider rather than reporting a false success.
4. Escalate the automation name, owner, activation time, last run/status, and provider status—not a secret or token.

**Limit:** Staff cannot infer that a schedule exists merely because an automation is listed.

### 13. Why does camera scanning fail, and what is the safe fallback?

Camera scanning requires HTTPS, a browser camera permission grant, and a supported detector. The app feature-detects the browser capability.

1. Confirm the page is HTTPS and allow camera permission for the site.
2. Reload the scanner after changing permission.
3. If the device/browser lacks the detector or permission cannot be granted, use the available ZXing/manual entry fallback.
4. Confirm the validated movement before saving: scanning alone does not mutate inventory.

### 14. Why is a customer token expired or a link revoked?

Customer payment-agreement, portal, review, and claim links are separately scoped, expiring/revocable tokens—not office login links.

1. Do not edit the URL or ask for the customer’s token.
2. Confirm which customer/job the link was issued for and whether it is expired or revoked.
3. An authorized staff member should issue a new supported link for the correct record. For claims, the move must be the linked completed move.
4. Report only the link type, record ID, and visible expiry/revocation message.

### 15. Why does a claim say approved but unpaid, or show a remaining balance?

**Approved** is a claim decision, not proof that money was paid. A remaining balance means the recorded settlement does not cover the approved liability.

1. Open **Claims** to confirm the claim status and approved amount.
2. Open **Claims & settlements** to inspect settlement records, external payout/reference, paid amount, and balance.
3. If a cash/repair/manual settlement was used, verify the owner-entered external payout/reference. It records accounting evidence; it is not proof that this app sent funds.
4. Do not mark the claim paid just because it is approved. Escalate mismatched amounts with claim ID, approved amount, settlement amount, balance, and reference.

### 16. Why are CSV/program dates or imported dates off by one day?

Date-only program and CSV values represent calendar dates, not UTC instants. A timezone conversion can display the wrong day.

1. Reopen the source CSV/program row and confirm the literal `YYYY-MM-DD` value.
2. Compare the workspace business timezone and the browser timezone.
3. Do not “fix” a date by adding or subtracting a day without checking the source record and job time block.
4. Escalate the file name (not sensitive contents), row/record ID, literal date, displayed date, and timezone settings.

### 17. What should I include when escalating?

Include enough to reproduce the guarded decision:

1. Workspace name, your role, page/sidebar label, and record ID.
2. Exact visible error/status text, including whether it says **blocked**, **ambiguous**, **uncertain**, **approved**, **paid**, **revoked**, or **stale**.
3. Action attempted, approximate timestamp, displayed date/time, workspace/browser timezone, and language/currency shown.
4. For dispatch: job date/time block, required skill/driver/truck/capacity, and the candidate resource name/ID.
5. For payments: invoice/payment/refund ID, amount and currency, gateway mode/status, and webhook/reconciliation state.
6. For messaging: channel, recipient record ID, consent state/source, provider outcome, and message ID if displayed.
7. For QBO: journal/request identity, local status, readback status, and whether the change was outbound or inbound.

Never include full card or bank data, passwords, API keys, OAuth tokens, webhook signing secrets, or an unredacted customer token.

### Current route and role reminder

Use the current sidebar routes, not stale provider shorthand: **Merchant gateway** is `/app/payment-gateway`, **Transactional messaging** is `/app/transactional-messages`, and **Claims & settlements** is `/app/claim-settlements`. The application also exposes **QuickBooks accounting** at `/app/accounting`; route visibility remains role-controlled. Provider activation, live credentials, live end-to-end tests, camera/device verification, and schedule registration are owner setup tasks, not evidence that those services are active today.

## First-use glossary

- **Workspace:** A company-specific CRM area. Its memberships, roles, and records are separate from other workspaces.
- **Role-aware sidebar:** Navigation that shows the tools assigned to your workspace role. A visible link does not override server-side permission checks.
- **Lead / customer:** A sales contact record. A lead becomes operationally useful only when its details and stage are saved; a customer record does not itself book a move.
- **Estimate / proposal / booked job:** An estimate calculates a prospective move; a proposal can be shared and signed; **booked** is a separate status explicitly saved by authorized staff before dispatch planning.
- **Preview:** A non-mutating server check or display. A preview must be followed by the relevant explicit save/confirm action when the workflow requires it.
- **Job clock:** The shared customer-billable arrival/departure clock. It is distinct from each crew member’s **Individual clock** for payroll review.
- **Verified ledger:** The saved invoice/payment record used to establish payment status. A hosted checkout page or return URL alone is not ledger evidence.
- **One-time token:** A link credential (for example, API key, portal, widget, review, claim, or webhook secret) shown once and intended to be copied immediately into approved secure storage.
- **Provider configuration:** Owner-controlled setup of external payment, messaging, accounting, or scheduler services. A screen or provider name is not evidence that the service is active.
- **Idempotency key:** A duplicate-protection value used for selected write operations. When a confirmation times out, retry the same action details rather than creating a different action.

## How to use this manual

Start with **Getting Started** to sign in, select the right workspace, and learn the role-aware sidebar. Then follow the operating flow appropriate to your work: sales and estimates → dispatch → field execution → finance, storage, and reporting. Use **Troubleshooting & FAQ** before repeating a blocked action or escalating an issue.

**Global operating rules**

- Confirm the active workspace and your role before creating, editing, or interpreting any record. Sidebar visibility is role-aware; server permissions remain authoritative.
- Use the exact current sidebar labels. In particular: **Merchant gateway** is `/app/payment-gateway`, **Transactional messaging** is `/app/transactional-messages`, and **Claims & settlements** is `/app/claim-settlements`.
- A preview, copied link, browser redirect, scheduled state, or success page is not automatically a saved business outcome. Read the page’s success/error notice and reload the record or ledger when the workflow says to verify it.
- Do not create workspaces, users, jobs, memberships, or financial records merely to explore. Do not paste card/bank details, credentials, API keys, webhook secrets, or customer tokens into notes or escalations.
- The **Language / Язык** selector changes interface labels and locale formatting between English and Russian. It does not translate customer-entered text, move dates, change stored money, or prove a provider’s state.

MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide > How to use this manual
Start with Getting Started to sign in, select the right workspace, and learn the role-aware sidebar. Then follow the operating flow appropriate to your work: sales and estimates → dispatch → field execution → finance, storage, and reporting. Use Troubleshooting & FAQ before repeating a blocked action or escalating an issue.

Global operating rules

- Confirm the active workspace and your role before creating, editing, or interpreting any record. Sidebar visibility is role-aware; server permissions remain authoritative.
- Use the exact current sidebar labels. In particular: Merchant gateway is /app/payment-gateway, Transactional messaging is /app/transactional-messages, and Claims & settlements is /app/claim-settlements.
- A preview, copied link, browser redirect, scheduled state, or success page is not automatically a saved business outcome. Read the page’s success/error notice and reload the record or ledger when the workflow says to verify it.
- Do not create workspaces, users, jobs, memberships, or financial records merely to explore. Do not paste card/bank details, credentials, API keys, webhook secrets, or customer tokens into notes or escalations.
- The Language / Язык selector changes interface labels and locale formatting between English and Russian. It does not translate customer-entered text, move dates, change stored money, or prove a provider’s state.

chunks.markdown:
### What this chapter covers

This chapter explains how staff sign in, choose a workspace, read the **Overview** dashboard, switch language, use the role-aware sidebar, and use the available **Settings** administration tools.

**Prerequisites and roles**

- You need a Manus account. The CRM uses Manus sign-in; there is no separate CRM password.
- A user with no workspace can create one. To work in an existing workspace, your Manus account must already be a member (or an Admin must link your already-signed-in account).
- Workspace roles are **Admin**, **Office admin**, **Sales & estimator**, **Dispatcher**, and **Field crew**. The server remains the final authority for permissions, so a visible menu item does not guarantee that an action will be accepted.
- Do not create a workspace, member, or test record merely to explore. Ask the workspace owner/Admin to perform setup when appropriate.

chunks.markdown:
### 1. Sign in with Manus

1. Open the team login page at `/login` (the public route is titled **Team login**).
2. If the session is still being checked, wait for **Checking your session…**. If you are already signed in, select **Open your workspace**.
3. If you are not signed in, select **Continue with Manus**. Complete the Manus sign-in flow.
4. Use **Back to home** to leave the login page. For help, use **Need a hand? Contact the crew**.
5. After sign-in, the login page identifies the account as **Signed in as {account}** and offers **Open your workspace**.

**Success state:** the workspace application opens and loads the selected company. If there is no selected workspace, the setup page appears instead.

**Note:** **Secure account login. No extra password to remember.** is an explanatory message, not a second login method.

Choose an existing workspace
chunks.markdown:
#### Choose an existing workspace

1. After Manus authentication, the application loads your memberships. The first available membership is selected by default unless a previously selected workspace is still valid.
2. In the left sidebar, select the current workspace button (building icon, company name, and your role).
3. In the menu, select the company you need. Each option shows the workspace name and your role there.
4. Wait for the application to reload. The workspace name in the top breadcrumb and the records on the page now belong to the selected company.

**Success state:** the active workspace button and the top bar show the new workspace; the sidebar role can also change because roles are membership-specific.

headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide

Create a new workspace
chunks.markdown:
#### Create a new workspace

Use this only when you are intentionally starting a new company workspace and have owner approval.

1. On **Set up your workspace**, enter a name in **Workspace name** (required; at least 2 characters). The placeholder example is **e.g. MoveFlew**.
2. Select **Create workspace**. The button is disabled until a non-blank name is entered and shows **Creating…** while saving.
3. The new workspace is selected automatically and the application reloads.

**Success state:** the new workspace opens empty. The page explicitly says that no demo customers are created.

**Limit—no self-service “join workspace” screen:** the current onboarding does not offer a join-code field or a general **Join workspace** action. If you need access to an existing company, ask its Admin to link your Manus account from **Settings → Membership** after you have signed in once (see the **Settings** instructions below). Do not create a second workspace as a workaround.

chunks.markdown:
### 3. Switch English/Russian and understand persistence

1. Find the language selector with the globe icon. On login and onboarding it is in the top area; inside a workspace it is in the top bar.
2. Open the selector labelled **Language / Язык**.
3. Choose **English** or **Русский**. This manual is intentionally written in English; the product selector can switch the interface to Russian.
4. The choice is saved in the browser, so it remains selected across reloads and later visits in that browser. Date/number formatting follows the selected locale (English uses the US locale; Russian uses the Russian locale).

**Tip:** if labels look unfamiliar, switch back to **English** before following this chapter. The language selector is available on the login, workspace setup, and workspace shell.

headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide

4. Navigate with the role-aware sidebar
chunks.markdown:
### 4. Navigate with the role-aware sidebar

The sidebar groups links and hides links that are not assigned to the current role. On a narrow screen, use **Open navigation**; close it with **Close navigation** or select a destination. The active destination is highlighted.

The current grouped labels and links are:

- **Workspace:** **Overview**.
- **Sales & customers** (office roles—Admin, Office admin, Sales & estimator, Dispatcher): **Leads**, **Sales pipeline**, **Estimates**, **Tariff engine**, **Communications**.
- **Moving operations:** **Jobs** (all roles); management roles (Admin, Office admin, Dispatcher) also see **Dispatch**, **Calendar**, **Warehouse scanner**, **Trip planning**, **Fleet & crew**, **Resource availability**, and **Storage**; office roles see **Inventory catalog**; field-enabled roles (Admin, Office admin, Dispatcher, Field crew) see **Field crew**; all roles see **Job documents**.
- **Finance & service:** management roles see **Move invoices**; finance roles (Admin and Office admin) also see **Billing & payments**, **Expenses**, **Payroll & tips**, **Claims**, **Merchant gateway**, **QuickBooks accounting**, and **Claims & settlements**.
- **Growth & insights** (office roles): **Reports**, **Marketing**, **Reviews**.
- **Administration** (finance roles): **Integrations & API**, **Transactional messaging**, **Automations**, **Settings**.

**Exact route notes for linked tools:** the sidebar’s current implementation uses `/app/payment-gateway` for **Merchant gateway**, `/app/transactional-messages` for **Transactional messaging**, and `/app/claim-settlements` for **Claims & settlements**. Use these links when opening the tools directly.

**Role-specific behavior to remember:**

- **Field crew** can see **Jobs**, **Field crew**, and **Job documents**, but the application blocks Field job sheets for an **estimator** with the message **Field job sheets are available to dispatch, office admins, and assigned crew members.**
- The dashboard’s **New estimate** action is not shown for **Field crew**.
- **Settings** is shown only to finance roles. Within it, Admin and Office admin can use pricing and sequence settings; a Dispatcher can use the membership tab as a read-only crew directory when the page is reached through an available route or permission.

chunks.heading: 5. Read the Overview dashboard correctly
headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide
1. Getting Started & Dashboard Navigation
5. Read the Overview dashboard correctly
chunks.markdown:
### 5. Read the Overview dashboard correctly

Select **Overview** (the dashboard route is `/app/dashboard`). The page heading is **Overview** and the caption identifies the selected workspace.

The four headline metrics are calculated from saved workspace records:

1. **Open opportunities** — customer records whose status is not marked won, closed, or inactive. The hint is **Customer records needing attention**.
2. **Scheduled moves** — jobs whose status is not complete or cancelled. The hint is **Across all upcoming dates**; this count is not limited to a chosen calendar range.
3. **Estimated revenue** — the sum of saved job `total` values. The hint is **From saved estimate totals**.
4. **Open invoice value** — the sum of each job’s `finalTotal` (or `total` when no final total is present) when the invoice status is not marked paid. The hint is **Based on invoice status**.

Use the dashboard panels as follows:

- **Revenue from saved jobs** groups job totals by move month, plus **Unscheduled**, and displays the most recent six groups. It says **Totals reflect estimates and completed invoices.** If there are no saved jobs, the success/empty state is **No revenue history yet**.
- **Upcoming moves** shows up to five non-complete/non-cancelled jobs whose move date is today or later, ordered by move date and start time. Select a row to open that job; use **All jobs** to open Jobs. If none qualify, the state is **No upcoming moves**.
- **Follow-ups** shows up to five incomplete reminders, with their due date/time. **Manage** opens Leads. If none are due, the state is **Nothing due**.
- **Dispatch readiness** reports the number of saved fleet vehicles and saved people records in the workspace. These are record counts, not a live statement that vehicles or people are currently available.

**Date semantics:** “upcoming” includes a move dated today and later. The dashboard does not provide a date-range picker. Revenue uses each saved job’s move month; an unscheduled job is grouped separately. The displayed date/time is localized by the English/Russian selector and the browser’s date formatting.

**Quick actions:** **View leads** opens Leads. **New estimate** opens the estimate creation route and is hidden for Field crew. These buttons navigate; they do not themselves save a lead or estimate.

chunks.heading: Pricing: maintain workspace rates
headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide
1. Getting Started & Dashboard Navigation
6. Use Settings for rates and team membership
Pricing: maintain workspace rates
chunks.markdown:
#### Pricing: maintain workspace rates

Pricing is for Admin and Office admin. It is labelled **Rates & materials** and explicitly says **Editable workspace configuration; this is not a published tariff.**

1. Select **Pricing**.
2. Review or enter the six mover-rate fields: **1 mover (no truck)** and the five remaining mover-count fields (the labels are generated as mover counts).
3. Review or enter **Minimum hours**, **Packing hourly rate**, **Weekend markup %**, **Travel per mile**, **Weight rate**, and **Mile rate**.
4. In **Material matrix**, review each material name and price. The current screen edits the existing rows; it does not provide an add/remove material control here.
5. Select **Save pricing**.

**What the button does:** it writes the complete rates/materials configuration for the active workspace and reloads the saved values. **Success state:** **Pricing settings saved.**

**Validation constraints:** the server requires exactly six hourly rates for one through six movers; rates and most amounts cannot be negative. **Minimum hours** must be from 2.5 through 24. Weekend markup is limited to 0–500%; the other rate fields have server maximums. If a value is rejected, read the displayed error and correct the field—do not assume a save occurred.

chunks.heading: Membership: view members or link a signed-in user
headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide
1. Getting Started & Dashboard Navigation
6. Use Settings for rates and team membership
Membership: view members or link a signed-in user
chunks.markdown:
#### Membership: view members or link a signed-in user

1. Select **Membership**. The **Workspace membership** table lists **Member**, **Role**, and the current member’s name/email.
2. Admins can change a member’s role using the role selector. The change saves immediately when the selector changes and the table refreshes.
3. Admins can use **Link signed-in user**. Enter the person’s address in the email field (placeholder **person@example.com**), choose a role, and select **Link member**.
4. The page reports **Membership link saved.** after a successful link and refreshes the member list.

**Required prerequisite:** the person must have signed in with Manus before an Admin can link the email. The screen says **People must have signed in before their email can be linked.** If not, the server returns **This user must sign in first before they can be added to the workspace**. An already-linked address cannot be added twice.

**Role and safety constraints:** only Admin can add members or change roles. Office admins can view the membership directory but cannot edit roles or add members. At least one workspace Admin must remain; the server rejects a change that would remove the last Admin. There is no remove-member control in this screen.

headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide

Troubleshooting and safe limits
chunks.markdown:
### Troubleshooting and safe limits

- **Workspace loading:** wait for **Opening your workspace…**. If an error appears, use the offered retry action rather than creating another workspace.
- **No workspace listed:** this means the signed-in account has no membership. Use the Admin linking procedure above; there is no join-code fallback in this implementation.
- **Wrong company data:** check the active workspace switcher and breadcrumb before editing anything. Workspace selection is persistent in the browser, and each company’s records are kept separate.
- **Missing sidebar item:** verify the current role and use the role-aware list above. Do not navigate by guessing an unavailable route.
- **Provider/configuration wording:** pages such as **Merchant gateway** and **Transactional messaging** are navigation tools/configuration areas. This chapter makes no claim that a payment, messaging, accounting, or other provider is active. Owners select providers and configure them later.

### 1. Create and maintain a lead or customer

1. In the sidebar, open **Sales & customers → Leads**. Alternatively, open **Sales pipeline** for a visual stage board.
2. Select **Add lead**. In the form, **Full name** is required. **Email**, **Phone**, **Source**, **Stage**, **Fit score**, and **Notes** are available; **Fit score** accepts 0–100. The normal initial stage is **lead**.
3. Select **Save lead**. The record returns to the saved list. To change it later, use the row’s **Edit lead** action and save again. Use **Add reminder** when a dated follow-up is needed; both the reminder title and **Due date & time** are required.
4. In **Leads**, use **Search name, email, phone** and **All stages** to narrow the list. The table shows customer, stage, source, score, and the next open reminder.

**Tip:** The separate **Sales pipeline** page searches name, email, phone, or source and adds a **Minimum score** filter. Drag a card to another column or use its stage selector; a successful move saves the customer stage immediately.

chunks.heading: 3. Build a quick estimate in four steps
headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide
2. Sales, Quotes & Lead Management
3. Build a quick estimate in four steps
chunks.markdown:
### 3. Build a quick estimate in four steps

1. Open **Sales & customers → Estimates → New estimate**. The wizard has four steps: **Customer & move**, **Exact route**, **Household inventory**, and **Pricing & proposal**.
2. **Customer & move:** enter required **Customer name**; add **Email**, **Phone**, **Move title**, **Move date**, and **Move size**. The available size choices are **Studio**, **Apartment**, **2 bedroom**, **3 bedroom**, **House**, and **Office**. Select **Continue**.
3. **Exact route:** enter **Origin address & ZIP** and **Destination address & ZIP**. Select **Get exact route**. On success, the wizard displays miles and minutes and uses them in pricing. If lookup fails, correct both exact addresses and retry.

   **Limit:** No substitute distance is invented when the Maps lookup fails. Do not rely on an unreturned route value.

4. **Household inventory:** search with **Find household items**, then use each item’s minus/plus controls. The running total shows cubic feet and pounds. The picker consumes the approved tenant catalog; quantities become part of the estimate.
5. **Pricing & proposal:** choose **Pricing method**: **Hourly local move** or **Long distance (weight + miles)**.
   - Hourly: set **Crew size**, **Hourly rate**, and **Estimated labor hours**. The configured minimum-hours rule applies to the calculation.
   - Long distance: set **Weight rate / lb** and **Mileage rate**; inventory weight and route miles feed the base amount.
   - Both methods support **Route travel fee**, **Packing labor hours**, **Packing materials**, and named **Accessorial name** fees. Enter a fee name (for example, a long carry), then enter its amount. The preview lists each fee. Add **Pickup / move notes** when conditions need to be recorded.
   - Review **Proposal preview** and **Estimated total**. A weekend adjustment can appear when configured for the workspace.
6. Select **Save & create proposal**. The button creates the job/estimate record and a shareable proposal token, then opens the saved job. **Saving** indicates the request is in progress; the saved job page is the success state.

### 4. Use a managed inventory catalog

Required fields are **Item key**, **Canonical item name**, **Room**, **Per-unit cubic feet**, and **Per-unit pounds**. **Item key** must contain only letters, numbers, underscore, or hyphen. **Important:** Volume and weight are per-unit planning estimates, not certified measurements or a guaranteed quote. Deactivating an item removes it from future picker choices; it does not silently rewrite an existing signed quote.

chunks.heading: 5. Review, copy, and send a proposal; understand booking
headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide
2. Sales, Quotes & Lead Management
5. Review, copy, and send a proposal; understand booking
chunks.markdown:
### 5. Review, copy, and send a proposal; understand booking

1. From **Estimates**, select **Open** on a saved estimate, or open the job from the estimate wizard’s success page.
2. On the job page, review **Move plan**, **Estimate**, and **Proposal**. Select **Open shareable proposal** to open the public proposal. The customer can review and e-sign there.
3. To share the link, select **Share proposal**. A success notice says **Proposal link copied.** If clipboard access is unavailable, copy the proposal URL from the browser address bar.
4. The Proposal card states **Customer e-signature received.** or **Awaiting customer signature.** A signature records proposal acceptance; it is not by itself a booking transition.
5. To change the operational status, choose **draft**, **estimate**, **booked**, or **cancelled** in the status selector and select **Save status**. Choosing **booked** is the actual booked transition and can queue the `job.booked` business event. It is not triggered by merely opening, copying, or signing the proposal.
6. **Assign dispatch** opens **Assign truck & crew** for management roles. It validates driver eligibility, skills, and schedule conflicts before saving. Assignment is operational allocation, not the sales-stage change.

**Limit — no automatic “customer signed = booked” action:** There is no separate customer-facing “book now” transition in this sales flow. After acceptance, an authorized office/management user must review the record and explicitly save **booked**.

chunks.heading: Preview and freeze
headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide
2. Sales, Quotes & Lead Management
6. Use the owner-attested Tariff engine (licensed profile workflow)
Preview and freeze
chunks.markdown:
#### Preview and freeze

1. In **Job selector**, enter a positive **Job ID** and select **Open job**. The route is `/app/tariffs?job=ID`; selecting a job only loads its current frozen revision.
2. Select an active profile and enter **Service date**, **Origin state**, **Destination state**, **Crew size**, **Estimated hours**, **Shipment weight (lb)**, **Distance (mi)**, **Trips**, **Travel miles**, **Stair flights**, **Elevator stops**, and **Elevator wait (minutes)**. Optionally enter **Heavy-item code (optional)** and **Heavy-item quantity**.
3. Select **Preview server quote**. Review **Preview line items**, effective ranges, approved hourly rate, minimum labor, and total. Preview alone never changes the job.
4. If the values or profile change, preview again. The **Freeze on unsigned job** button is enabled only when the current preview matches the current inputs and the job is not signed/completed.
5. Select **Freeze on unsigned job**. The success notice states that a frozen tariff revision was applied to the unsigned job and linked draft estimate. The resulting **Current frozen snapshot** shows revision, profile version, lines, and total.
6. If a snapshot already exists, check **I intentionally want a new revision of the existing frozen quote.** before creating a deliberate revision. Later profile or approved-rate edits do not rewrite the frozen snapshot.

**Hard constraint:** If the job is signed or completed, the screen displays **Signed or completed — changes blocked** and tariff changes cannot be applied.

7. Quote embed widget, keys, UTM, and public links
chunks.markdown:
### 7. Quote embed widget, keys, UTM, and public links

1. Open **Administration → Integrations & API** and use the **Embed forms** tab. A widget requires an active **widget** access key. Select **Create access key**, enter required **Name**, choose **Kind: widget**, and select **Create key**.
2. A widget key is restricted to `leads:create`. After creation, copy the one-time token, **Browser-relative link**, and **Iframe code (uses this browser origin)** from the secret dialog. The success dialog says the token cannot be retrieved again; select **I copied it** only after storing it in the approved secure location.
3. The public route is `/quote/<one-time-token>` and is titled **Embedded quote intake**. The widget creates a lead request; it does not book a move or create a signed estimate by itself.
4. UTM and custom attribution are canonicalized on the saved lead through the fields in **UTM and custom tracking**: `source`, `medium`, `campaign`, `content`, `keyword`, `adGroup`, and `customTracking`. Review or correct these fields on **Lead details** after intake.

**Limit — origin controls:** The current **Embed forms** UI provides the key, relative link, and iframe code based on this browser origin; it does not expose a separate staff-facing allowed-origin list. Do not promise domain allowlisting that is not shown.

chunks.heading: 8. Customer portal, inventory review, invoices, and deposits
headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide
2. Sales, Quotes & Lead Management
8. Customer portal, inventory review, invoices, and deposits
chunks.markdown:
### 8. Customer portal, inventory review, invoices, and deposits

1. In **Integrations & API**, select **Create access key**, choose **Kind: portal**, and select the required **Bound customer**. Portal keys must be customer-bound and expose only that customer’s data. The fixed scopes are `portal:read` and `portal:inventory:submit`.
2. Select **Create key**, then copy the one-time **Browser-relative link** from the secret dialog. The public route is `/portal/<one-time-token>`; the **Portal links** tab lists the bound customer but intentionally does not reveal the token again.
3. The customer portal can show **Jobs and proposals**, **Invoices and balances**, **Storage**, and **Documents and recorded terms**. A customer can select **Open proposal** for a linked proposal.
4. Under **Inventory for staff review**, the customer selects a **Linked job**, adjusts quantities for the canonical items already on that job, and selects **Submit for staff review**. A success notice states the selection was submitted; it does not change a signed estimate or booking.
5. For an invoice with an eligible balance (at least the implementation’s minimum checkout amount), the portal offers **Pay in TEST checkout**. It opens a test checkout in a new tab.

**Limit — deposit/invoice reality:** The portal exposes linked invoice balances and TEST checkout, not a separate “deposit invoice” creation button in this sales chapter. Returning from TEST checkout does not mark an invoice paid; only a verified payment webhook updates status. Owners must configure the merchant provider later; do not claim that payment is live or that a deposit was collected.

headingPath: MoveFlew — User Operating Manual & Help Center Guide
